Dr. Anthony Fauci’s lawyer was ordered removed from a heated Senate hearing after he tried to speak in defense of the infectious disease expert, who is refusing to answer questions about the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic as part of what he described as a years-long partisan crusade intended to smear him.

Fauci’s lawyer, David Schertler, was escorted from the room after the Senate Homeland Security Committee’s Republican chair Rand Paul warned of “consequences” and “repercussions” for Fauci’s refusal to testify on Wednesday.

“You are not invited here for testimony, sir. You are being disruptive. Would you behave this way in a courtroom? No, because the judge would put you in jail,” Paul told Schertler as he tried to speak. “I can’t do that today, but I can have you escorted from the premises.”

Paul said the hearing is “not a game with his lawyers.”

"Security, please remove him from the room,” he said.

open image in gallery Dr. Anthony Fauci’s attorney David Schertler was removed from a Senate hearing after trying to speak in defense of the infectious disease expert, who was reprimanded by the Homeland Security Committee’s Republican chair Rand Paul for his refusal to testify ( Reuters )

After his brief opening remarks, the 85-year-old former National Institutes of Health official invoked the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution and declined to answer the committee’s questions.

“Given Senator Paul’s obvious obsession with calling for my prosecution, his repeated slanderous comments about me, and recently, his publicly releasing my personal diary aimed at embarrassing and intimidating me, is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something, anything, that can vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up in his words, quote, ‘behind bars,’” Fauci said.

“Any person who has followed his unhinged obsession with me would come to the same conclusion,” he continued.

“Although it pains me to say so, and because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of the federal government … under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right to the Fifth Amendment to refrain from answering your questions,” Fauci said.

Democratic members of the panel have stated that Paul is wrongly seeking to trap Fauci in a potential misstep that could lead to perjury charges.

Paul later defended his decision to eject Schertler from the hearing.

“You don’t get to do that. That’s one thing you give up when you take the Fifth Amendment,” he said. “You don’t get to put your lawyer forward to justify. You can do it in the press. ... He was out of order and it was appropriate to have him ejected.”

In a statement to The Independent after the hearing, Schertler said it was “outrageous for Senator Paul to exclude his counsel for making a legitimate legal point” by trying to state that Fauci has a valid right to assert a Fifth Amendment privilege.

“It proves the baseless and vindictive nature of this proceeding and Rand Paul’s personal vendetta against Dr. Fauci,” he said.

During a round of probing questions from Paul, Fauci repeatedly answered: “On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution.”

Fauci, who steered the nation’s initial response to the COVID-19 pandemic, has previously testified to Congress under oath about the pandemic’s origins, including questions from Paul and Senate Republicans who have sought to publicly grill Fauci on whether the outbreak began with a lab leak in Wuhan, China.

This week, in his latest escalation of a yearslong feud, Paul released more than 1,000 pages of Fauci’s personal records, including his notes during Donald Trump’s response to the pandemic and entries detailing his efforts to counter the president’s false statements. Trump’s Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr said he shared the documents with Republican members of the Senate panel.

open image in gallery After he was sworn in, Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment and refused to testify to the Republican-led committee about the origins of the COVID-19 pandemic ( AFP/Getty )

Under the first Trump administration, Fauci contradicted the president and officials over mitigation efforts and unproven treatments and a refusal among Republicans to address the seriousness of the public health threat, which killed more than one million people in the U.S.

Despite the speed and efficacy of the Trump administration’s vaccine development, Fauci has attributed the difficulty of a comprehensive response to the rapid mutation and contagion of the disease against a backdrop of patchwork public health infrastructure, conflicting guidance and the politically volatile, anti-science and partisan response.

In April 2021, Fauci wrote that members of the “radical right wing” like Paul were trying to “connect me with the virus from WUHAN.”

“They are saying that I deliberately worked with the Chinese together with [zoologist] Peter Daszak to create a virus that would be released to the world,” he wrote at the time. “This sounds very much like a way-out conspiracy theory, which it is. However, there are enough crazy people around to make this a problem.”

The following month, he wrote that the conspiracy theory was evolving again thanks to “the usual cast of characters.”

Fauci, who was preemptively pardoned by Joe Biden, has repeatedly denied allegations of a cover-up. Critics have accused Paul and his allies of abandoning oversight responsibilities during the Trump administration to pursue an ideological crusade despite outbreaks of cyclospora and measles across the U.S. and a lethal Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

“No credible evidence has been produced to support these absurd charges,” a group of more than 150 scientists and physicians wrote in an open letter in defense of Fauci on Tuesday. “These conspiracy theories have led to a five-year period of harassment and threats of violence directed at Dr. Fauci and his family.”

Infectious-disease experts have also insisted to Paul and other Republicans that while the National Institutes of Health funded virus research in Wuhan, that work could not have sparked an outbreak.

Trump and his allies, however, have embraced the narrative. The Trump administration created a website that claims the “true” origin of the pandemic was the result of a lab leak without sharing any definitive evidence.

open image in gallery Fauci, who has vehemently rejected ‘conspiracy theories’ among Republican officials, has repeatedly clashed with Paul, who has used his position on the committee to investigate Fauci ( AP )

Paul, who has spent years using his position on the panel to investigate Fauci and the origins of the pandemic, said in his opening statement that Fauci should “come clean” and “ask for forgiveness” to ensure “a man-made epidemic never happens again.”

Fauci, according to Paul, has spent years “avoiding responsibility.”

“There will be another pandemic. There will be another crisis,” he said. “They will invoke science as if it’s a commandment.”

As public support for the nation’s institutions declines under a health agency that elevates conspiracy theories, public health officials “have it backwards,” according to Paul.

It is “secrecy,” “arrogance,” “censorship” and a "refusal to admit error” that destroys public trust, Paul said.

Fauci had previously denied that the National Institutes of Health directly funded gain-of-function research — in which a studied pathogen is altered to make it more transmissible in an effort to better predict emerging diseases and combat them with vaccines — at a Wuhan lab that has been scrutinized as a possible source of the disease.

In 2022, the GOP senator suggested Fauci, who was serving at the time as the chief White House medical adviser and director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, had lied to Congress over whether the agency supported such research.

“Senator Paul, you do not know what you’re talking about, quite frankly, and I want to say that officially,” Fauci said at the time. “You do not know what you’re talking about.”

Sen. Gary Peters, the top Democrat on the panel, slammed Paul for leading a hearing that “looks backwards.”

“We are instead litigating the past,” he said Wednesday.

While “COVID-19 exposed serious deficiencies in our nation’s public health infrastructure,” the committee is avoiding asking “forward-looking, life-saving questions” to “better prepare Americans when the next emergency occurs.”

Kiyoshi Kurosawa, the acclaimed Japanese director often hailed as "the master of horror," was initially worried about how viewers would react to his first samurai film but his concerns proved unfounded.

The Samurai and the Prisoner, set to premiere in New York and Los Angeles on July 31 before a wider U.S. release throughout August, garnered an enthusiastic reception at its Cannes Film Festival debut in May.

The film is already proving to be Kurosawa’s most popular work to date, following its successful earlier release in Japan. This marks a significant achievement for a director whose extensive filmography includes the 2020 Venice Film Festival’s Silver Lion-winning Wife of a Spy and the 2008 Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize winner Tokyo Sonata, a poignant exploration of family conflict.

Despite his prolific career, Kurosawa admits to a persistent sense of wonder about his craft.

open image in gallery Yuriko Yoshitaka in a scene from The Samurai and the Prisoner ( Janus Films via AP )

"Filmmaking remains a mystery for me," he said, describing it as a complex endeavor that merges the tangible world being filmed with the intangible narrative that must be conveyed.

"I don’t understand it. And that’s why I keep making films," he told The Associated Press in a recent online interview from New York, adding that he constantly questions why he cannot emulate the likes of Yasujiro Ozu or Alfred Hitchcock.

Kurosawa’s previous works, such as his 1997 film Cure, which features Koji Yakusho as a detective pursuing a serial killer, are typically characterized by a chilling creepiness that unfolds within ordinary settings. Yet, the samurai genre inherently establishes a fictitious, otherworldly realm where everyday normalcy is absent, a departure Kurosawa acknowledged.

The Samurai and the Prisoner delves into a rivalry between warlords, employing the familiar Shakespearean plot twists common to samurai films.

Kurosawa explained the genre's core elements: "There is, first of all, power. A feudalistic society is built on a hierarchical relationship of those at the top and those at the bottom. Then there’s betrayal."

open image in gallery Masahiro Motoki in a scene from The Samurai and the Prisoner ( Janus Films via AP )

He added, "People try to grab power, and in so doing get thrown into confusion. That exists in any society, historically and perhaps even today. And so this is also about what’s eternal."

Tackling a samurai movie presented Kurosawa with new challenges, including the fundamental task of directing actors in a genre where, unlike modern dramas, there were no predefined parameters for line delivery. He also faced the common wisdom that directors venturing into new territory risk alienating fans, compounded by the fact that the traditional samurai genre, or "jidaigeki," is increasingly unfamiliar even to many Japanese audiences.

However, once production commenced, everything seamlessly fell into place. The authentic sets, costumes, props, wigs, and makeup collectively transported the actors to the film’s otherworldly setting. Kurosawa was fortunate to film in historic temples and castles across Kyoto. The movie retains his signature long shots and almost claustrophobic dialogue scenes, where a palpable tension builds, promising an impending, unimaginable horror.

His latest work embodies the aesthetic of an orthodox samurai film, staying true to the genre’s legacy of depicting the horrors and pathos of war. It even features wide shots of armored warriors on a hilltop, reminiscent of Akira Kurosawa’s Ran and Kagemusha, though the two directors are unrelated.

open image in gallery The film is already proving to be Kurosawa’s most popular work to date, following its successful earlier release in Japan ( Janus Films via AP )

Kiyoshi Kurosawa found the experience of making The Samurai and the Prisoner so enjoyable that he hopes to direct another samurai film, this time incorporating more spectacular sword-fighting sequences akin to the Zatoichi series. He also expressed interest in exploring new genres, perhaps even a musical.

He pledged to continue making horror films, provided audiences aren't weary of his distinctive style, which often features prolonged periods where "nothing appears to be happening."

He voiced concern that his slow-burn approach might seem dated in an era where popular films, both in Japan and globally, are characterized by a rapid succession of explosive events designed to keep viewers on the edge of their seats.

"A scary thing generally doesn’t happen every five minutes in my films," Kurosawa noted, concluding, "But if that’s OK, then I’d like to make my film."

The names and phone numbers of thousands of school leaders, university staff and government officials have been leaked onto the dark web after the Department for Education (DfE) was hacked.

Online thieves reportedly stole 607,000 records in the attack, including full names, job titles and email addresses of people who have engaged with the department.

According to The Times, which first reported the breach, the hackers targeted the DfE help desk, which manages requests from local authorities and school leaders, as well as records from the Turing Scheme – the database education institutes use to oversee UK students who study overseas.

However, DfE sources told The Independent the data protection risk to those affected is not considered high, noting that data obtained includes different sets of data which cannot be connected.

They are understood to have reported the incident to the Information Commissioner’s Office, and is working with the National Crime Agency (NCA) and National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC).

open image in gallery Around 607,000 records were reportedly taken in the attack ( Getty )

The department is understood to be fixing the help desk portal and the Turing scheme portal following the hack, and has switched telephone communication while maintenance work is done.

Dark web posts seen by The Times reportedly shows a cybercriminal group called ExfilSquad claiming responsibility for the breach.

Jake Moore, an adviser at leading European cybersecurity firm ESET, warned that government agencies are “soft targets” for cybercriminals, arguing that this attack “isn’t a one off”.

He said: “Government agencies often lack proper funding and consequently may not have the best protection for their systems, making them soft targets for cybercriminals. With weaker security, government agencies and departments can also get unintentionally caught up in a net of ransomware attacks when other companies are targeted.

“The issue is this isn’t a one off and the UK government should be learning from its mistakes. There are now multiple examples of government and local government agencies being struck in similar attacks which often lead to weeks of disruption and have a huge knock-on effect to wider communities.

“When information like this is stolen, criminals can still do a lot by piecing together a data jigsaw and even creating convincing follow up phishing emails to lure people into clicking into malicious sites. It’s best to remain vigilant to any unsolicited communication.”

A Department for Education spokesperson said: "We have robust processes in place to protect information and took swift action to contain this incident. The information involved is limited to customer service contact details relating to individuals and organisations. No other data has been accessed.

"We continue to work closely with the National Cyber Security Centre and the National Crime Agency.”

News.title: Gen Z is investing - but in these risky areas instead of building security in pensions
News.content:
Almost 780,000 Gen Z investors have entered the market in the past two years, but many are starting with cryptocurrencies rather than diversified funds or pensions.

Vanguard estimates that more than a third (37 per cent) of Gen Z investors began investing during this period, compared with 11 per cent overall. One in three chose cryptocurrency as their first investment, ahead of individual company shares or investment funds.

Separate GWI research suggests this appetite for hands-on investing may be developing at the expense of retirement saving.

Gen Z ownership of gold increased by 50 per cent over six years, while ownership of stocks and shares rose by 45 per cent and crypto by 43 per cent. Pension ownership among the age group fell by 10 per cent over the same period.

The figures point to a financially engaged generation drawn to assets that feel accessible and under their control. The danger is that short-term excitement distracts from the employer contributions, tax relief and decades of compounding available through a workplace pension.

Why risky assets are winning attention

Investment apps make it possible to buy cryptocurrency, gold or part of a share within minutes. Social media adds stories of rapid gains, while pensions can feel remote and difficult to understand.

Sarah Coles, head of personal finance at AJ Bell, said: “FOMO can hit hard at times like this, especially when money is tight and the thought of getting rich quick is hard to resist.”

Those gains can disguise the difference between investing for decades and speculating on an asset whose price may move sharply.

open image in gallery ( Getty/iStock )

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Get a free fractional share worth up to £100.

Capital at risk. Terms and conditions apply. Go to website 

Coles said: “It’s incredibly difficult to time the markets - especially when the price is based largely on so many other speculators - so you could end up buying and selling at the worst possible times and losing significant sums.”

Individual shares carry concentration risk too. Their performance depends on one company, while a diversified fund can spread money across hundreds or thousands of businesses.

What pension savers stand to lose

Many workers may not think of their pension as investing.

Anna Macdonald, investment strategy director at Hargreaves Lansdown, said: “On the other hand, people may already be investors, but not know it - according to an HL survey, only 47 per cent of people actually know their pension is invested in the stock market.”

A workplace pension usually invests contributions in funds holding shares, bonds and other assets. It also comes with financial help unavailable through an ordinary investment account.

Coles said: “Pensions have huge advantages from day one, because in a workplace pension, when you pay in, your employer will pay in, and the government will top it up with tax relief.”

Under minimum automatic enrolment contributions, an employee usually pays five per cent of qualifying earnings and an employer pays at least three per cent. For a basic-rate taxpayer, tax relief means every 80p paid personally becomes £1 before the employer contribution is added.

“If more people understood that they could basically double their money in a day, pensions might get more love,” Coles said.

AJ Bell calculated that somebody paying £100 a month into a pension from age 25 to 68 could build £238,509, assuming annual growth of seven per cent and charges of one per cent.

open image in gallery ( Getty/iStock )

Waiting five years would reduce the projected pot to £172,870. A ten-year delay would cut it to £123,820. These are illustrations rather than guarantees, but they show how difficult it can be to recover lost time.

Ian Futcher, financial planner at Quilter, said: “Pensions are ultimately long-term savings vehicles. There is a good chance you won’t need to touch this money for 30, 40 years or perhaps even longer.”

How to combine control with security

Younger savers do not have to choose between a pension and investments they can access earlier.

The first priorities are usually clearing expensive debt and building an emergency fund. Workers should then consider paying enough into their workplace pension to receive the full contribution available from their employer.

Money for goals at least five years away can also be invested through a Stocks and Shares Isa, which can be accessed before retirement. A diversified portfolio of funds can form the core, with a smaller amount reserved for individual shares, gold or crypto.

Macdonald said: “If people do want to allocate some of their investment pot to a more speculative investment, they should make sure it’s only a small portion and that they fully understand the risks before going ahead.”

Coles added: “If they’re really keen to dabble in risky investments, they should be prioritising those long-term investments, but they can still put a small proportion of their cash into these speculative assets - on the understanding they could lose it all.”

Gen Z’s willingness to invest early could become an advantage. It becomes a retirement trap when control and excitement replace pension benefits that are difficult to recreate elsewhere.

When investing, your capital is at risk and you may get back less than invested. Past performance doesn’t guarantee future results.

News.title: Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC
News.content:
Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

News.title: Recovery aids and building muscle: Welsh weightlifter Laura Hughes answers your questions
News.content:
Laura Hughes first discovered weightlifting while training at her local Crossfit gym, making the transition from amateur gym-goer to competitive lifting.

Now a member of the Welsh national weightlifting squad, the 33-year-old holds the Welsh record for both the snatch and the clean and jerk (the two official competitive lifts in weightlifting) and is currently third overall in the women’s Welsh rankings. Hughes won bronze at this year’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, following on from her third place at the 2018 Games in Australia.

We caught up with her for our Readers Ask series, where industry specialists answer questions from our Telegraph Recommended Reader Panel.

Who inspired you to get into weightlifting?

Olamilekan, South East

Originally, it was lots of different people, particularly general gym goers who were doing weightlifting at my gym. As I’ve grown as an athlete and become more competitive, I’ve had other inspirations.

Most notably, coming into [the Commonwealth Games], it has to be Gareth [Evans], our coach. Looking back at his performance in 2018 when he won his gold medal is so inspiring. [English lifter] Emily Godley was another competitor in 2018. She won the gold medal in my category and I just remember thinking that she was on fire that day.

What are the best exercises for you to build muscle mass?

Norman, Wales

We spend a lot of time doing our main lifts, so snatches, clean and jerks, but we also do lots of pulls and squats. I spend a lot of time doing accessory work to make sure that my body stays healthy, especially being an older athlete. I’ve put on quite a lot of muscle in this last block just from going heavier and pushing my limits with my main lifts.

What advice would you give to people who want to improve their strength?

David, North West

The most important thing is consistency. As long as you’re doing something, do it regularly, even if it’s twice a week. Don’t be afraid of picking up some dumbbells. If you’ve got somebody that can teach you how to lift weights properly, that’s going to be the best option. Do it safely, do it consistently, and don’t be afraid to try new strength exercises.

News.title: Explosive mpox outbreak causes 3,000 cases in Madagascar
News.content:
More than 3,000 cases of mpox have been recorded in Madagascar after the virus spread from a single port city to some of the country’s busiest coastal hubs.

A total of 3,022 cases and 20 deaths have been recorded as of this week, with cases in Toamasina and Taolagnaro accounting for more than half of all diagnoses.

The outbreak has been linked to Clade 1b mpox, a strain that emerged in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2024, prompting the World Health Organization (WHO) to declare a global public health emergency at the time.

“The main factor driving the continued spread of the disease is human mobility, seeding new outbreaks in areas where the virus has not circulated before,” Professor Carlos Maluquer de Motes of the University of Surrey told The Telegraph.

“Under-reporting is likely, with the real number of cases exceeding what is being reported.”

News.title: Chelsea in 10-goal thriller as ‘Alonso ball’ brings risk and reward
News.content:
Chelsea’s first match under the management of Xabi Alonso was a 10-goal thriller in Australia, as the Premier League side eventually showed their class in a 6-4 win over Western Sydney Wanderers.

Star striker João Pedro, who was controversially left out of Brazil’s World Cup squad, scored a nine-minute hat-trick after coming off the bench with half an hour of the friendly remaining.

Alonso had selected a youthful team for the first hour before bringing nine senior players, including João Pedro, into the side in the second half. According to Transfermarkt, Chelsea’s squad is valued at over £1.3bn while their opponents a more modest £5.86m.

Teenage signing Dastan Satpayev, midfielder Dario Essugo and winger Jamie Gittens also found the net for Chelsea, who were defensively vulnerable for long spells for the game.

Here are five things Telegraph Sport learned from Alonso’s first match.

João Pedro picks up where he left off

João Pedro scored 13 goals in the second half of last season and his impressive performances resulted in the 24-year-old being named Chelsea’s player of the campaign. It was something of a surprise, then, when he was left out of Carlo Ancelotti’s Brazil squad this summer.

The good news for Chelsea is that João Pedro’s absence from the World Cup has given him plenty of time to recover ahead of the new campaign, and he looked thrillingly sharp in his second-half performance against Western Sydney Wanderers. The difference in class between João Pedro and Liam Delap, the man he replaced, was clear for all to see.

Two of the Brazilian’s three goals were classy, composed finishes — and he also created a goal for Gittens after surging past three defenders on the left wing. João Pedro looks like he means business.

News.title: China’s chip breakthrough triggers global tech rout
News.content:
China has achieved a breakthrough in developing technology crucial to the AI boom, overcoming US efforts to limit Beijing’s access to the systems.

China’s chip giant Shanghai Yuliangsheng has started production of deep ultraviolet lithography machines, according to The Information, a tech publication.

These machines, which can reach the size of a double-decker bus, use high-powered lasers to imprint designs on to silicon wafers, which are used to make chips.

Until recently, only Western companies and allies of the US had the capability to produce these machines.

The most advanced versions of the technology have largely been the preserve of companies such as Dutch giant ASML and Japan’s Nikon.

These machines have been cut off from China by US export controls, preventing their production of advanced chips as Washington seeks to slow the development of AI in the country.

Semiconductor stocks plunged on the report. Trading was briefly halted on South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index after it suffered a collapse of nearly 11pc overnight, following a bleak day on Wall Street.

Advanced semiconductors, such as those used in AI chips, rely on minuscule circuits, invisible to the naked eye. They can only be manufactured by directing tiny lasers onto microchip wafers, a process known as ultraviolet lithography.

News.title: Ramsay-Peaty ‘human first, athlete second’ as he settles for second bronze
News.content:
So a pair of bronze medals for the man who once only dealt in gold. Not that Adam Ramsay-Peaty thinks that is necessarily such a bad trade when he also computes the wider price of sporting domination.

“I’ve been that person who wins all the time, and it costs you pretty much everything, and I won’t say it’s worth it,” Ramsay-Peaty said after his return to international competition continued in his now favoured 50m breaststroke with a second podium place at these Commonwealth Games. “That period of time, where I was undefeated for eight years, it was athlete first, then human,” he added. “Now it’s human first, then athlete, which is a very fair price to pay.”

Aged 31, and with a baby girl on the way with wife Holly Ramsay, Ramsay-Peaty’s order of priorities might be understandable, but it was still another performance to raise questions over whether he can again climb to the top of a major podium.

Swimming is not kind to the over-30s – Michael Phelps was the first man in 2016 to win an Olympic gold in the pool even at the age Ramsay-Peaty is now – and we still have another two years until the Los Angeles Olympics. It would be the greatest achievement even of the Englishman’s extraordinary career to win his third individual Olympic title.

He trailed from the start here and was almost exactly a second outside his world record – set almost a decade ago – as Australia’s Sam Williamson completed a breaststroke double ahead of South Africa’s Michael Houlie in second. “As you get older, it gets harder,” said Ramsay-Peaty, before adding a crucial caveat, “but I’m enjoying it more…in my head, I’m getting fresher.”

News.title: Musk passed ‘slow death sentence’ on HIV patients by cutting US spending, says head of UNAIDS
News.content:
The world’s richest man has passed a “slow death sentence” on an untold number of people with HIV by cutting US spending on the disease, according to the head of UNAIDS.

In an interview with the Telegraph, Winnie Byanyima, executive director of the UN body, said Elon Musk’s claim that the cuts made to US aid had resulted in “zero” deaths was born of ignorance.

“I do not know where Elon Musk gets his data from, but he [is] showing ignorance of the disease”, Ms Byanyima told the Telegraph at the opening the 26th International Aids Conference in Rio de Janeiro.

“This disease is not like a bullet shot in the head and you die. This is an attack on the immune system.” Withdrawing medication is a “a slow death sentence,” she said.

Data released by UNAIDS show that reductions to international funding and cuts to HIV prevention and community services threaten a resurgence of the epidemic.

In 2025, 1.2 million more people became infected with HIV and 570 000 more people died of Aids-related illnesses as the world fell short of global targets.

Although new HIV infections and Aids-related deaths are at their lowest levels in more than 30 years, an 18 per cent cut to total international funding means previous gains are now at risk, say experts.

Sports.title: UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan
Sports.content:
UEFA issue new statement as Gianni Infantino sends threat over World Cup plan

UEFA are firmly opposed to Gianni Infantino and FIFA's controversial plan to sell shares in its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors and have issued another statement

View 2 Images FIFA is at war with UEFA (Image: Pau BARRENA/AFP via Getty Images)

UEFA has issued a second statement criticising FIFA's plan to sell off the World Cup, saying that the scheme is designed to 'enrich themselves and their friends'. It comes ahead of an emergency UEFA meeting which will see European football chiefs discuss FIFA President Gianni Infantino's plan to sell shares in its competitions to private investors.

‌



After the plans were leaked on Tuesday, UEFA issued a statement claiming that FIFA had 'crossed a line'. Now, further reports say that FIFA has written to its 211 member associations promising $40m (£30m) if they back the controversial plan.

‌



It's added that the members have until September 19 to respond positively - or else they will not get to access an initial $20m (£15m) by January 1. UEFA have said that the deadline 'says everything you need to know about this plan'.

‌



A statement read: "Today we have learned of FIFA's deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA's scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends.

"We can grow the game correctly. It's time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans."

‌



At the upcoming emergency meeting, UEFA could discuss boycotting the World Cup in what would be a drastic move. UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin missed the men's final earlier this month amid tensions with FIFA. The next World Cup on the calendar is the women's edition in Brazil next year.

It should be noted that FIFA is a not-for-profit organisation and is owned by its 211 members. FIFA therefore enjoys a tax-free status in Switzerland, where its headquarters are located.

FIFA insist that, in the event of outside investment, it would retain sole control over football governance, its competitions and the international match calendar, as well as all sporting and regulatory decisions. It adds that the investment would go into a FIFA subsidiary rather than FIFA itself.

‌



Should UEFA boycott the World Cup? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin recently boycotted the men's World Cup final (Image: Toya Sarno Jordan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Infantino commented in FIFA's announcement - made after its plan was leaked: "Football is the world's most popular sport and an extraordinary engine of human and social development.

Article continues below

"Parts of the game have turned that popularity into remarkable commercial value - and we celebrate that success and want it to continue, because it lifts the whole game ... our next stage of growth needs a structure built for it, one where the commercial side of the game operates as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world."

Sports.title: Abandoned EFL stadium set to be demolished 18 years after former club left
Sports.content:
Abandoned EFL stadium set to be demolished 18 years after former club left

The ground is in a sorry state after falling into disrepair

View 3 Images Millmoor has been largely untouched since Rotherham United left in 2008 (Image: Getty Images)

An abandoned EFL ground could finally be demolished, almost 20 years since it last hosted a men's football match. Millmoor was the home of Rotherham United from 1907 until 2008 and hosted some of the club's most memorable moments.

‌



Due to disputes over the ownership and redevelopment of the ground, the Millers left the stadium in 2008 with a view to building a new ground in the town. They moved temporarily to the Don Valley athletics stadium in Sheffield, an unloved venue because of its running track.

‌



The club eventually bought land close to Millmoor to build their new home, the 12,000-capacity New York Stadium, which opened in 2012. Meanwhile, Millmoor, which is clearly visible from the new ground on the other side of a railway line, has remained largely untouched since 2008.

‌



It looked set to get a second life in 2024, when it was spruced up by Ken Booth Jr, the son of long-time owner Ken Booth. The site was revamped and cleared of debris so it could be used by local junior teams and the Doncaster Belles women's team.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

But two years on, the historic venue could now be torn down after the ground's owners, CF Booth, entered administration, with the Ron Hull Group acquiring Millmoor.

‌



Liverpool chief provides FSG investment update after Jeff Bezos talks READ MORE :

Man Utd enter advanced talks for striker transfer with £30m clause proposed READ MORE :

A statement by the Ron Hull Group, issued via the Rotherham Business News, read: "The buildings and structures selected in the current application to demolish are all in a poor condition due to years of neglect and are suffering from a general lack of maintenance, specifically elements like roof finishes and the structures themselves.

"It is assumed this situation accelerated in the period since Rotherham United Football Club vacated the site.

View 3 Images The abandoned stadium had been left to the elements (Image: Ben Booth/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



"The current main stand is only partially completed, and has been exposed to the elements since at least 2007.

"The high cost of repair, yet alone proceed to complete this stand would be excessive given that there are very limited numbers of possible users of the ground. Thus meaning it is unbuyable."

View 3 Images The ground could be no more by early next year (Image: Ben Booth/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

‌



If the demolition plan is approved by the local authority, the Millmoor Lane and Railway stand, plus adjoining buildings, will be levelled, with work expected to conclude by the end of January 2027.

The Millers are preparing for life in League Two after suffering relegation from League One last season.

Sports.title: Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer
Sports.content:
Brentford confirm Jordan Henderson exit as shock Chelsea transfer edges closer

Jordan Henderson had one year left on his contract with Brentford, but the club have agreed to terminate his deal in order for him to join Chelsea on a free transfer

View 2 Images Jordan Henderson is on his way to Chelsea (Image: Adrian Dennis/AFP via Getty Images)

Brentford have announced the departure of Jordan Henderson, paving the way for him to join Chelsea. Henderson, 36, is poised to move to Stamford Bridge on a free transfer after Brentford agreed to terminate his contract.

‌



The former Liverpool captain signed a two-year deal with Keith Andrews' side in July 2025 but has cut short his stay after a single season. As Brentford confirmed his exit, Henderson said: "I leave Brentford with a lot of gratitude for the opportunity the club gave me, and for the support and care shown to me and my family from day one.

‌



"Coming back to the Premier League was really important to me, and Brentford gave me that chance. I'll always be thankful for that. I hope I was able to play my part in helping the team through an important period for the club. We achieved a lot together last season, and it’s something everyone involved should be proud of.

‌



"Brentford is a special football club. It's ambitious, progressive and full of good people. From the owners and leadership, to the coaching staff, the players and everyone behind the scenes, it's been a privilege to be part of it.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest READ MORE :

"Most of all, I'd like to thank the supporters. Their backing never changed, and the connection they have with the club is clear to see. They care deeply about Brentford and they support the team in the right way every step of the journey.

‌



"Finally, thank you to Matt (Benham, owner), Phil (Giles, director of football), Lee (Dykes, technical director) and Keith, every member of staff, and all my team-mates. It's been a pleasure to work alongside you, and I'll look back on my time at Brentford with a lot of pride and some great memories."

Henderson made 36 appearances for Brentford, helping them secure a ninth-place finish in the Premier League. The midfielder had spent the previous 18 months at Ajax following a spell in Saudi Arabia which came after 12 trophy-laden years at Liverpool, winning both the Premier League title and one Champions League trophy.

Andrews commented: "Following the departure of our club captain Christian Norgaard to Arsenal, and with Vitaly Janelt not fit enough to start the season, Jordan was a really important signing for us because he added elite-level experience.

"He played a big part in some memorable performances, especially in the early part of the season as we were forming a new team. He had an insatiable desire to represent England at the World Cup in the summer and it was always part of the plan for us to discuss the next chapter for him and what it looked like.

"Taking into consideration Jordan's ambitions and where our squad is currently, we both felt it was the right time for Jordan to pursue his career elsewhere. It's been a pleasure working with Jordan and I sincerely wish him every success."

Sports.title: Vinicius Jr's agent gave transfer advice as Arsenal plot move for Real Madrid superstar
Sports.content:
Vinicius Jr's agent gave transfer advice as Arsenal plot move for Real Madrid superstar

Vinicius Junior has been linked with a sensational move to Arsenal, with his agent's words shedding light on his future

View 2 Images Vinicius Junior's agent made a telling statement about his future (Image: Getty )

Vinicius Junior’s agent once named the Premier League as the only league the Brazilian would realistically leave Real Madrid for. Arsenal have emerged as stunning favourites to land the 26-year-old superstar if he opts for a move away from the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



The Brazilian's contract expires next year and he is no closer to signing a new deal, though talks surrounding the winger’s future are being held this week. Reports emerged last weekend that Vinicius is a target internally at Arsenal, with football.london stating the Gunners are willing to break the bank for the forward if he becomes available. The huge financial cost of the transfer is understood to not be an issue either.

‌



So far, Arsenal’s interest is in its early stages with no contact made yet with Los Blancos. It remains to be seen whether the Premier League champions bid for Vinicius, who is eligible to open pre-contract talks with clubs outside of Spain from January over a free transfer in the summer of 2027.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mikel Arteta could be forced to break his own Arsenal rule in major transfer U-turn READ MORE :

A move to north London would come as a huge shock given the calibre of the player and just how important Vinicius has been to Real Madrid’s success in recent years, having played a key role in two Champions League triumphs.

It was once inconceivable that he would ever leave the club which announced his signing as a 16-year-old - that much was clear from the words of Vinicius’ long-time agent, Frederico Pena, back in 2023.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Pena said: "Vini is very close with Real Madrid and he’s so happy there. He’s very at ease, he loves the club. He’s been there so long, he’s kind of turned into a man there."

View 2 Images Arsenal are favourites to sign Vinicius Junior if he leaves Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

But while Pena said he did not expect Vinicius to change clubs in the near future and insisted he could stay as a Madrid player for the rest of his career, he did not rule out a transfer to the Premier League.

‌



"I can’t really see that [a Premier League move] happening right now," Pena added. "But who knows, these things change in football and there’s things you would never imagine seeing that happen. I would just say if he were to leave Real Madrid some day, it would make no sense for it to be somewhere other than the Premier League.

"But will he one day leave Real Madrid or will he be a one-club kind of player? I would tell you right now there’s a big chance that he's the kind of player who stays in one club and makes history there and stays there for 15-plus years."

That suggests he would have sufficiently advised the player and made him aware of the benefits of joining the Gunners. Arsenal’s current status as champions makes them hot favourites in England to land the Brazil international.

Article continues below

Vinicius has scored 128 goals and notched 100 assists in 376 appearances for Los Blancos so far. Meanwhile, Arsenal have already made three signings this summer in Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Christos Tzolis.

Sports.title: UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed
Sports.content:
UEFA handed blow as Gianni Infantino's controversial World Cup plan backed

Gianni Infantino has received some public support for his radical World Cup plan by a president from one of FIFA's 211 member associations

View 2 Images FIFA president Gianni Infantino plans to make huge changes to the World Cup (Image: (Photo by Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images))

Czech Republic FA president David Trunda has revealed he supports Gianni Infantino's controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup's commercial rights. The organisation have proposed plans to set up a different $20bn (£15.5bn) company to run its competitions, with 20 per cent of that then offered to external investors.

‌



Other leading figures and governing bodies in football, including UEFA, have hit out against the idea. However, that has not stopped Mr Trunda, who became the Czech FA's president last year, backing the plan.

‌



He told Sky News: "I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team. Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

‌



UEFA nations could BOYCOTT World Cup in light of FIFA's plot to sell tournament READ MORE :

That aforementioned new company would be called 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' with Infantino making it clear to FIFA's 211 member nations that if they sign up before September 19, a $40m (£30bn) windfall would be theirs but failure to do so after that date would result in them receiving a fraction of that sum.

UEFA and the FA are among the organisations to have released public statements on the controversy with the latter stating they were "deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved".

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



"When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further," they added.

UEFA wrote that the plan "crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross". It added: "The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football: it is not FIFA's to sell."

View 2 Images Nasser Al-Khelaifi is firmly against Gianni Infantino's World Cup plans

‌



Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaifi, who is also part of the French club's ownership group, is the latest high-profile name, in collaboration with beIN and Qatar's sports investments, to speak out ."We urge for calm and thorough consultation... with more rigorous and transparent governance processes," a statement read.

Glenn Micallef, who is the European Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport, also issued a clear statement on X where he he expressed concern over FIFA being "aligned with the financial interests of private entities".

On the other hand, the Czech FA president added: "I was elected a little more than a year ago, and for me personally all the projects I have experienced in cooperation with FIFA have been very positive for the development of European football."

Liverpool forced to change pre-season plans as Reds hit with travel chaos

Liverpool are due to play Wrexham in New York on Wednesday during their pre-season tour of the United States, with Andoni Iraola's squad having planned to arrive the night before

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola's preparations have changed (Image: Ian Horrocks/Sunderland AFC via Getty Images)

Liverpool will land in New York just hours before kick-off in Wednesday's friendly against Wrexham after the club's pre-season tour was hit with travel chaos. The Reds' flight from Chicago was cancelled on Tuesday due to adverse weather conditions.

‌



As a result, Andoni Iraola's squad have been forced to change their plans and will now only arrive on the day of the game. Liverpool are based in Chicago during their tour of the United States and returned there after Saturday's 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville.

‌



But ahead of their second friendly, thunderstorms and heavy rain meant that they were unable to arrive in New York on Tuesday as planned. Not only has the cancellation affected Iraola and his players' preparations, but also the reveal of Liverpool's new away kit.

‌



Several first-team players were scheduled to attend an event at Brooklyn's Skylight at the Refinery to show off Adidas' latest product. Instead, Liverpool legends Ian Rush and Robbie Fowler stepped in to model what the Reds will be wearing on the road in 2026-27.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool's clash with Wrexham will be played at Yankee Stadium, the home of baseball's New York Yankees. The stadium holds 47,309 fans and it's a special ground to Iraola.

‌



In 2016, the Spaniard ended his playing career with New York City FC, who the stadium is also home to. Despite an injury to Joe Gomez in Nashville, Iraola will have a bigger squad to choose from.

Ryan Gravenberch, Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have all returned to training, although they may not be involved this early into their respective pre-seasons. "The three players that are going to join us are going to be [in the] second week fully with us," Iraola told a press conference last week.

"Individually, I talked with the three of them, they know the main things, but I am looking forward to having them here with the group and to go slowly, slowly with recovering bodies [to the squad]."

‌



Meanwhile, Alisson Becker, Cody Gakpo and Virgil van Dijk will start their individual programmes at Liverpool's AXA Training Centre in Kirkby while their team-mates are stateside. "They will, in terms of dates of training, be very similar but they will start training at the AXA in Liverpool," Iraola confirmed.

"Because of different reasons, especially Virgil because he has been the player with most minutes in Europe I would say, and Cody for other reasons, they are going to start training basically in the same week as the others but instead of making them come here with the team, we considered that it was sensible with them to start the first week training with a small group or even with younger players that are at the AXA and join us when we [return]."

Sports.content:
Kelly Cates makes thoughts clear on Gabby Logan and Mark Chapman as she opens up on BBC job

Match of the Day presenter Kelly Cates has revealed what she thinks about her BBC colleagues

View 3 Images Kelly Cates has spoken about her Match of the Day colleagues (Image: The Romesh Ranganathan Show/YouTube)

Kelly Cates insisted she hadn't read any reaction to her Match of the Day appointment as she revealed her true thoughts on co-hosts Gabby Logan and Mark Chapman. Last season was the first of a new presenter line-up, with Cates, Logan and Chapman sharing hosting duties after long-running anchor Gary Lineker stepped down.

‌



The trio, who also led the BBC's World Cup coverage, host Match of the Day on a rotation basis, with Cates and Chapman continuing to work for Sky Sports and Logan and Chapman fronting the Sports Agents podcast together.

‌



Cates, the daughter of Liverpool icon Kenny Dalglish, was honoured to take on the prestigious role, especially alongside fellow respected broadcasters Logan and Chapman. She told The Romesh Ranganathan Show: "They [the BBC] just asked me. There was no big manoeuvring. Gary was leaving, which accelerated it slightly, and the process came a bit quicker.

‌



"They said, 'Do you want to come and do it, we're looking at a team of three.' I was like, 'Who are the other two?'

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"They said it was Mark and Gabby and I said, 'That's amazing.' It's Match of the Day, so it sells itself. Also, the fact it's those two…Normally, I take the p*** out of the people I work with and it's OK.

‌



Mark Chapman's BBC colleagues have all told World Cup host exactly what they think of him READ MORE :

"But it's Mark and Gabby, and they're amazing. Being on a team with them is genuinely really exciting. I feel like I'm in a great little group."

The trio's appointment has generally gone down with viewers, not that Cates would know, as she shields herself from coverage, whether it is positive or negative. She added: "I didn't read it, and that's not hard to do.

View 3 Images Cates shares hosting duties with Mark Chapman and Gabby Logan (Image: BBC/Charlie Clift)

‌



"It's not hard to avoid the coverage. It's hard to stop people sending you the coverage but I just tell them I don't want them to send it to me, even nice stuff. I still really have no idea what people thought about it or think about it. I just do my job."

The new presenting line-up has coincided with a fall in Match of the Day's viewership. However, that is believed to be due to a change in viewing habits, with digital highlights clips of each Premier League match now available at 8pm on Saturdays.

View 3 Images The trio replaced Gary Lineker, who is now focusing on his podcast empire (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

‌



Average weekly views for the highlights across the iPlayer, the BBC Sport website and the app stood at 1.52million between August and December 2025. That has more than offset the drop-off in those viewing the traditional programme.

Between August and December 2024, the average weekly viewing figures across all devices – both TV and iPlayer and the Saturday and Sunday shows – was 7.65m, but were down to 6.88m across the same period last year, a drop of around 770,000.

Sports.title: O'Neill promises more Celtic signings | McGregor: Where I want to be
Sports.content:
Martin O'Neill insists there is "no question" that Celtic will make more signings this summer, but he wants "quality rather than quantity".

The Scottish Premiership champions have brought in Camilo Duran and Kasper Hogh so far, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain returning on a new one-year deal.

Supporters have been frustrated by the club's lack of transfer activity, while influential striker Daizen Maeda has left to join newly-promoted Premier League side Ipswich Town.

Celtic begin their title defence against Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports, ahead of their Champions League play-off later this month.

But manager O'Neill is urging some patience from fans.

"We're trying to get some quality into the football club," the 74-year-old told Sky Sports News.

"We've lost Daizen, he was a big, big player for us and so we have to replace him. I think that we're doing our best to do that.

"We will get some more players in, there's no question about that, but I want quality rather than quantity."

Image: Camilo Duran has joined Celtic on a five-year deal

After a rollercoaster campaign that saw O'Neill return to the club twice, Celtic clinched the title in a final-day decider against Hearts in May.

And O'Neill wants the players to take some lessons into the new campaign.

"Last season was terrific, it's gone now, it's consigned to history. Now we're ready to go," he added.

"I think it was mentality as much as anything else that got us over the line.

"It was strong, it was a will to win and we saw it through.

"That will be very, very important this season, there's no question about that."

McGregor: Where I want to be

Meanwhile, Callum McGregor has reiterated that Celtic is "where I want to be" amid ongoing speculation linking the long-serving captain with a reunion with former boss Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah in Saudi Arabia.

The 33-year-old said in April he wanted the club to match his ambitions if he was to stay on as they laboured towards the Scottish Premiership title.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Celtic captain Callum McGregor discusses his future, hope for signings and the Champions League target | Watch Celtic vs Dundee, live on Sky on Monday

"Listen, this is a football club that's been part of my whole life since I was eight, nine years old. It's where I want to be. It's where I want to play football," he said.

"Ultimately, I want to keep driving everything that I possibly can to make sure this club is successful. Then eventually, the day that you do leave it, you want to leave it in a really good place."

Asked if he felt the club were matching his ambitions, McGregor said: "Yes, listen, we've signed two strikers, two really good players. Obviously, they've come in and done really well.

"Big Kasper (Hogh) has just joined us over the last 24 hours. It's good signs, it's positive steps and that is to add to what is a really good group already.

Saturday August 1: Falkirk vs St Mirren (3pm)

"I spoke about this at the end of the season as well. I don't really think there's a group of players and a group of staff that could have got us through that difficult moment as much as these boys did.

"It's obviously about trying to add bits of quality, but what we do have here is guys who want to work for the club, who are good footballers, who want to get better and ultimately did bring success to the football club during a difficult season, so we have the makings of a really, really good team.

"Obviously, the standard for us is trying to get to Champions League football. That's where we want to be. It takes the club to a different level. So, can we keep pushing as players, staff and our football club to make sure we get there?"

Celtic begin title defence against Dundee

Celtic begin their Scottish Premiership title defence at home to Dundee on August 3, live on Sky Sports.

The Monday night clash, which will kick-off at 7.30pm, rounds off a groundbreaking opening weekend that will see all six top-flight games shown live on Sky Sports for the first time.

Sports.title: Ko reveals plan to 'channel inner Foxy' in push for more major glory
Sports.content:
Lydia Ko wants to "channel her inner Foxy" and push for more New Zealand major success at the AIG Women's Open, having been reduced to tears by Ryan Fox's win at The Open.

Fox claimed a dramatic one-shot win at Royal Birkdale earlier this month, where a final-hole birdie saw him become only the third men's major champion from New Zealand.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment New Zealand's Ryan Fox won The Open with a 12-foot birdie on the final hole

The 39-year-old's win was the first New Zealand success at The Open since Bob Charles lifted the Claret Jug in 1963 at Royal Lytham & St Annes, the same venue where Ko will chase a fourth major title and second AIG Women's Open victory.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the final round of The Open, where Fox claimed a dramatic victory at Royal Birkdale

"I would love to keep the dice rolling," Ko said in her pre-tournament press conference. "Super-excited for Foxy [Ryan Fox] and the whole of golf in New Zealand for his win just up the road at Royal Birkdale.

"I don't think I've been that nervous and that excited watching somebody else play. Just his whole back nine and the way he played over the weekend was incredible.

"It would be cool to channel my inner Foxy and his fearlessness out there these next few days."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The best of Fox's winning round at The Open, where a two-under 68 saw him complete major victory

Fox had been eight strokes off the halfway lead before equalling men's major history with a third-round 62, leaving him two back heading into the final day. He then birdied two of his last three holes to close out the major victory.

"I went to go work out and everywhere I went I was like 'please turn on The Open'," added Ko, who was watching Fox's win from the west coast of the USA. "It ended up not working on the TV, so I had it on my cell phone.

Image: Lydia Ko is looking to win her fourth major title the AIG Women's Open

"I can't remember my workout at all because my whole focus was there. I took an Uber ride back home. As soon as I got home he was on the 18th - when I saw that drive I was relieved but so excited, super-pumped.

"I went in, I closed the door and I screamed. My husband ran out and was like 'what's happening?' Ten seconds later, I was just crying. It was emotional for me. I can only imagine what it was like for him!"

Image: Ko's last worldwide win was at the 2025 HSBC Women's World Championship

Ko missed the cut in the first two women's majors of the year before recovering from a slow start to the KPMG Women's PGA Championship to finish tied-15th, then shared seventh at the Amundi Evian Championship.

The 29-year-old plays alongside Nelly Korda and Haeran Ryu - both multiple major winners in 2026 - over the first two rounds at the AIG Women's Open, with Ko aware of the challenging test ahead as she looks to lift the trophy for a second time in three years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ko carded a final-round 69 to claim major victory in the 2024 AIG Women's Open at St Andrews

"I think it [winning] would be very special," Ko said. "I think this is the toughest Women's Open I have ever played. I don't know what I thought when I played in 2018 - might have been in a lot of bunkers that are on the golf course that are in my memory bank.

"It actually feels like a very new course to me. I know they made a little bit of adjustments on a couple of the holes, but it's a hard golf course. Even on a pretty perfect day it's playing hard. So when you win on that kind of calibre of golf course, I think it's always something that you come off feeling extra proud.

"With Foxy having won The Open, I think it [winning] would be very meaningful and I think very empowering for golf in New Zealand."

Sports.title: Tottenham beat Sydney FC on penalties after stunning Tel free-kick
Sports.content:
Tottenham beat Sydney FC on penalties to earn their third victory of pre-season after being held to a 1-1 draw over 90 minutes during which Mathys Tel scored a stunning free-kick.

Tel found the top-right corner with a wonderful strike from 25 yards in the 29th minute in Sydney, but the A-League side equalised after half-time through Takahiro Sekine before Martin Dubravka saved a penalty in the shoot-out, which allowed Dane Scarlett to net the winner.

Tottenham are interested in signing Manchester City winger Savinho and Tel, who only signed for the club permanently this summer in a £30m deal from Bayern Munich, appeared to respond to those transfer links with a stand-out 45-minute display off the left.

How Spurs lined up Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Dubravka; Tye Hall (Robertson, 65), Hardy (Tingey, 78), Davies (Takai, 46), Kyerematen (Byrne, 78); Gray (Donley, 65), Bergvall (Tonali, 46); Solomon (Yang, 65), Gallagher (Melia, 65), Tel (Williams-Barnett, 46); Richarlison (Scarlett, 65)

Unused subs: Kinsky, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Ajayi.

Rested key players: James Maddison, Dominic Solanke, Destiny Udogie, Micky van de Ven, Kevin Danso, Jan Paul van Hecke.

Roberto De Zerbi rested a host of his stars, including Mateus Fernandes, but started midfielder Lucas Bergvall, who Sky Sports News understands wants to leave the club this summer, for his first pre-season minutes before he was replaced at the break by club-record signing Sandro Tonali.

Andy Robertson made his first Spurs appearance as a second-half substitute, being handed the captain's armband and impressing in a 25-minute cameo by setting up two chances and having a shot saved before tucking away a penalty.

Who is missing from Spurs' pre-season tour? Mohammed Kudus, Xavi Simons, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert and Guglielmo Vicario did not travel due to injury.

Rodrigo Bentancur and Pape Matar Sarr were granted extended leave following their appearances at the World Cup, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Djed Spence won't take part having reached the latter stages of the tournament.

What we learned from Spurs' friendly with Sydney...

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

Tel responds to Savinho news - Spurs are after a new left winger, and Man City's Savinho could be another high-profile addition to Roberto De Zerbi's squad. But Tel provided a reminder of his talents. His stunning free-kick stole the show but he was also Spurs' brightest attacker in the game. If Savinho and Tel are Spurs' two left-wing options, it shows real depth in that area.

Robertson looks energised on debut - He only got 25 minutes, but Andy Robertson made a real impact on his first Spurs outing. The left-back should have had two assists but Min-Hyeok Yang missed from close range. De Zerbi's full-backs in this game were very attacking and often had good goalscoring chances, is the Scot in line for a new wave of attacking influence in the Premier League?

Image: Richarlison challenges for the ball

Gray could be important for De Zerbi - When the team news came out, it was a surprise to see Archie Gray named as captain for the second pre-season game in a row. More experienced players such as Conor Gallagher, Richarlison and Ben Davies also started, but it was the young midfielder with the armband. Despite all the talk about Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali coming in, is Gray the final piece of that three-man midfield, on the basis of that vote of confidence from De Zerbi?

Where are Spurs' goals coming from? Yes, it's only pre-season. But you look at the Spurs attack and wonder where the goals are coming from. Spurs were wasteful against Sydney - with Gallagher missing three big first-half chances and substitute Yang missing two more after coming on. Richarlison was anonymous in his 60-minute display, while the likes of Dominic Solanke, James Maddison, Mohammad Kudus, Xavi Simons and Dejan Kulusevski are still out injured. De Zerbi has made loads of signings in defence and midfield, but more still needs to be done up front.

Sports.title: Infantino offers £30m incentive for FIFA members to back controversial plans
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino has given football associations until September 19 to back his plan to sell off part of FIFA to private investors with a £30.1m ($40m) incentive to accept, a letter has revealed.

FIFA announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments.

Under the proposal, FIFA would raise up to £3.1bn ($4.2bn) from external investors by selling minority, non-controlling stakes in FFE, which it says would be valued at around £15bn ($20bn).

The governing body says its plans - which need approval from member associations - could deliver more than £7.53bn ($10bn) in "football development funding" over the next four years.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville, Andy Burnham, the FA and more react to Gianni Infantino's World Cup sale plan

The FIFA president, in correspondence sent only to the 211 member associations after his secret plans were leaked and met with fierce opposition from UEFA, raised the subject of finances that would be available from January.

He warned that countries will have access to much less cash for development projects, grassroots football and national teams if they do not back selling off more than 20 per cent of a new commercial spin-off to oversee World Cups.

Infantino said the launch of FFE needs more than 50 per cent of members to back the plans, along with his ruling council.

He wrote: "Should neither condition be satisfied, FIFA will continue as planned with the Forward Programme 4.0 … meaning approximately £7.5m ($10m) per MA [member association] for the next cycle."

Infantino raised the prospect that associations that do not back his plans could miss out on the cash if the majority of the world endorses the venture.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Prime Minister Andy Burnham disagrees with FIFA's attempts to bring in private investment for the World Cup

He wrote: "A singular and unique funding opportunity only for those Member Associations who wish to participate, with their decision to be made by September 19 2026 so we can plan ahead and with funds to be available immediately as of January 1 2027."

The letter raises the financial stakes, with FIFA previously saying on Tuesday that the new venture would provide access to funding of £15m ($20m) from 2027 to 2030 - a figure that has now doubled.

Infantino wrote: "This entity will be fully focused on one target objective; generating as much value as possible for FIFA's Member Associations."

But FIFA has not commented on how much Infantino stands to benefit financially from delivering a £15bn ($20bn) venture - and how he could stay on beyond 2031 when term limits require him to relinquish the presidency if re-elected next year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky News sports correspondent Rob Harris raises the prospect of the World Cup being boycotted due to FIFA's attempts to bring in private investment

Threat of a boycott and 'deep concern' from the FA

UEFA, European football's governing body, issued a furious statement on Tuesday, saying the proposals "crossed a line".

An emergency virtual meeting of UEFA's 55 member associations will take place on Thursday to discuss opposition to FIFA's controversial idea and Sky Sports News understands there is a willingness to use the threat of a boycott if Infantino pushes ahead with the plans.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham voiced his criticism on Tuesday evening, saying on X: "Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine."
