Alderweireld continued: "It was not an easy period because when I arrived, I think it was five or six years ago that they arrived in the Champions League. So I think sometimes it needed time.

"And I think we were getting there. Before Spurs were happy, we were top four, happy. But Pochettino changed everything.

"They said, 'Look, we're not only competing to get in the top four, we're competing for winning the title.' Of course, we were not ready yet. But you saw us taking steps.

5 Tottenham gave everything to make the Champions League final in 2019, but came up short in Madrid Credit: getty

"And of course, it was not easy as well to go to Wembley [for the 2017/18 season to finish construction on their new stadium].

"It was not our home to change stadiums. But still, we did well. And sometimes you need a little bit of luck.

"But I think that the season that Chelsea won the league, I think we had the most points ever for us as a Spurs team.

"So sometimes you need a little bit of luck as well. And we didn't. But yeah, I think we set a new standard for Spurs.

"And of course, everyone's talking, he didn't win a trophy, he didn't win a trophy. But if you see how we played games, that we competed for the top four and the title, I think that was a big change for Spurs."

5 Chelsea have not won the Premier League title since the 2016/17 season Credit: AFP

Best player Alderweireld played with?

In addition to his star-studded Spurs dressing room, the 127-cap international also played with Kevin De Bruyne and Eden Hazard for his country - with Belgium finishing third at the 2018 World Cup.

The most underrated among them was Dembele, who Harry Kane once listed as the most naturally gifted player he played alongside.

Walker labelled the midfielder as one of the greatest, with Antonio Rudiger listing him as his toughest opponent, and John Arne Riise admitting he couldn't believe Dembele never played for Real Madrid or Barcelona.

Asked who would be the best that he played with, Alderweireld told talkSPORT: "It's a name that everyone is saying.

"And everyone is always a little bit surprised. But the best player that I ever played with was Mousa Dembele. 100 per cent.

5 Tottenham fans and players knew how good Dembele was even if he went under the radar of rivals Credit: Getty

"He was so good. He was really strong. If he had the ball, you couldn't get it off of him.

"The only small thing he lacked was maybe shooting to the goal.

"But the other parts, defensively, everything, and how good the guy is. Yeah, he's my top number one.

"When you play big away games, and there is pressure on you, for example, Chelsea away, City away.

"He's the guy in midfield who asks for the ball, and you can play to him. Because some players, they play hide and seek.

"They ask for the ball, but not really asking for the ball. But he's the guy who asks for the ball and says, give it to me, and I will do something, and I will help.

"As a defender...especially when clubs put pressure on you, you know, 'Oh, this is a guy who can play the ball to, and he will hold it for me'."

Dembele left Tottenham in 2019 to move to Chinese Super League club, Guangzhou City, before retiring from playing in 2022.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino puts Premier League return on hold with new US Soccer contract close
Sports.content:
After a disappointing end to the World Cup, Mauricio Pochettino will get the chance to go again for the United States with a new deal imminent

Mauricio Pochettino puts Premier League return on hold with new US Soccer contract close

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to lead the USMNT to another World Cup.

After a period of reflection following defeat to Belgium in the Round of 16, talkSPORT understands an extension to his contract with the US Soccer Federation is close to being agreed, keeping him in charge until the 2030 World Cup.

3 Pochettino has reportedly committed his future to the USMNTthrough to the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

The former Southampton, Tottenham, PSG and Chelsea coach from Murphy in Argentina, signed a reported $6million a year deal in September 2024 to lead the United States into the 2026 World Cup on home soil.

That two-year deal - funded in part by investment companies and commercial partners - was due to expire after the World Cup, and the manner of a 4-1 defeat to Belgium placed huge questions over the 54-year-old staying on.

Those doubts were raised even further when former USMNT defender Steve Cherundolo was announced the head US head coach for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles.

However talkSPORT understands Pochettino is expected to be involved in LA2028 in some capacity as part of his lucrative deal.

Pochettino's focus will be on the full squad as the expected new four-year deal will take in the next COPA America in 2028 and the World Cup in 2030 that will take place in Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola had been heavily linked as possible replacements for Pochettino but other options appear thin on the ground.

Klopp has answered the call from his native Germany while Guardiola is likely to take an extended break from the game after stepping down as Man City manager.

Instead Pochettino stays on, and must deliver a return on a contract that makes him one of the best paid international managers on the planet.

So far he has a fourth-place finish in the Nations League, a runners-up finish in the CONCACAF Gold Cup and yet another Round of 16 World Cup defeat for the US, on his resume.

How did the USMNT do at the World Cup?

A rollercoaster World Cup campaign on their own soil had hopes high of just a second appearance in the quarterfinal stages since 1930.

3 The USMNT enjoyed a strong campaign at the World Cup, up until they reached the RO16 Credit: Getty

3 Pochettino is determined to lead the USMNT at the next World Cup Credit: Getty

Two wins from their first two games wrapped up first place in the group before their final game which brought a much changed team and a defeat against Turkey.

But that decision was justified when the US eased past Bosnia & Herzegovina in the Round of 32 in Santa Clara to have expectation at fever pitch.

However the build up to a Round of 16 meeting with Belgium was dominated by the fallout red card to Folarin Balogun in the win over Bosnia.

A one-game suspension was suspended, seemingly on the intervention of President Donald Trump, and Balogun played.

However the US were crushed at Seattle's Lumen Field and their hopes of a deep run extinguished to crank up the pressure on Pochettino.

Sports.title: ‘Nuclear-powered’ Man United ace who could have stopped Lionel Messi is ultimate cult hero
Sports.content:
‘Nuclear-powered’ Man United ace who could have stopped Lionel Messi is ultimate cult hero

The Premier League has had its fair share of superstars pass through the door over the years.

Yes, they are usually the ones who score all the goals, shatter records and put bums on seats up and down the country.



6 Ronaldo stands as one of the greatest players to have featured in the Premier League Credit: Getty

But every club over the years has welcomed a player who, for whatever reason, became a terrace icon.

Perhaps they were a one-season wonder, or scored an unforgettable goal that lives long in the memory of fans.

No matter their exploits, they all did something that earned them cult hero status.



But who are the best cult heroes in Premier League history?

Well, Jamie O'Hara and Jermaine Pennant decided they would take it upon themselves to name the Premier League cult hero XI in the latest episode of the Encouraging Signs podcast.

However, there was a catch.

Only one player from each club was allowed to be in the line-up, ensuring as many teams as possible were represented.



Goalkeeper

This player's unique outfit choice made him unmistakable on a field.

In a sport where every player wears shorts, Gabor Kiraly dared to be different.

Instead of following the trend, the Hungarian donned a pair of grey tracksuit pants.



6 Kiraly was better known for his pants than his goalkeeping ability Credit: Getty

"I tried shorts during my spells in Germany and England but it didn't suit me," Kiraly said in 2015 regarding his fashion choices.

"The end result is more important than your look."

Kiraly's stint as a Premier League player was short but sweet, featuring 32 times for Crystal Palace in the 2004/05 campaign along with five games for Aston Villa two seasons later.

Defenders

Nadir Belhadj may have been a Portsmouth player for just two seasons, but it was enough to earn him cult hero status with the Fratton Park faithful.



The Algerian initially joined on loan in the summer of 2008 but Pompey were so convinced by the defender, they made his move permanent in January 2009.

He was part of the Portsmouth squad that reached the FA Cup final in 2010 and to get there, he bagged a goal against the club's bitter rivals Southampton.

Joining Belhadj in the cult hero backline is Neil Ruddock, better known as 'Razor' Ruddock, or the 17th 'hardest footballer of all time'

Any player who is better known by their nickname is always going to be a cult hero, especially when they 'took a dump' in a toilet that once belonged to former Iraq president Saddam Hussein.



Playing for the likes of Southampton, Tottenham and Liverpool throughout the 90s, Ruddock never shied away from a crunching challenge or the opportunity to wind up a rival, even the great Eric Cantona.

6 Campo's hair was unmistakable on the pitch Credit: Getty

Rounding out the defence in the Cult Hero XI is Ivan Campo.

Yes, that defender who moved from Real Madrid to Bolton in 2002 and remained with the Trotters until 2008.

Such was the curly-haired defender's influence, an English indie folk band named themselves Ivan Campo in his honour.



Midfielders

Few midfielders to have graced the Premier League were as mad as Thomas Gravesen.

Gravesen joined Everton in 2000 and was sold to Real Madrid in January 2005, but what happened in between was the stuff of cult hero legends.

Whether it was setting off fireworks at Everton's training ground, shooting a paintball gun at his teammates, driving around Merseyside in a Nissan Micra or his passionate displays on the pitch to whip Goodison Park into a frenzy, Gravesen's stint with the Toffees was the stuff of a true cult hero.

Although he was nowhere near as eccentric as Gravesen, Manchester United fans will never forget the on-field impact of Park Ji-Sung.



The ex-Manchester United midfielder may as well have had a third lung, such was his remarkable endurance.

6 Park never shied away from the big challenges Credit: Getty

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

Even Andrea Pirlo, who Park famously man-marked when United played AC Milan in the Champions League round of 16, remarked in his autobiography: "The midfielder must have been the first nuclear-powered South Korean in history, in the sense that he rushed about the pitch at the speed of an electron."

His manager, Alex Ferguson acknowledged not unleashing him on Lionel Messi was an error on his part in the 2011 Champions League final, which they lost 3-1.



"That’s where I lost the final against Barcelona at Wembley," he said in 2021. "I should have changed at half-time and put Ji-Sung Park on Messi. That was a mistake.

“I realised after 10 minutes… I was going to do it at half-time and I thought that if we could just equalise before half-time they might see the game differently and we may grow into the game better.

“We were actually quite good in the last 10 minutes of that half anyway, we came into it and we could have been in front actually. But if I’d played Ji-Sung Park against Messi, I think we’d have beaten them. I really do.

“Messi with two highlights, the fantastic goal he scored and he made the other one. He was a great player, but if there was a great player who was going to do it [stop him] it was Ji-Sung Park.”



Providing the width in the team was Damien Duff, who enjoyed spells with Blackburn Rovers, Chelsea, Newcastle and Fulham.

6 Payet was named in the PFA Team of the Year following his debut season with the Hammers

Duff's time at Stamford Bridge was his most successful, winning two Premier League titles along with the League Cup.

Never the flashiest or the trickiest, 'Duffer' won over Chelsea fans with his tireless work ethic and team-first mindset.



On the left wing, O'Hara and Cundy could not look past Dimitri Payet.

The Frenchman's 2015/16 campaign with West Ham was the stuff of legends, as he registered nine goals and 12 assists to help the club finish seventh.

His technical ability was wizard-like and few will forget the free-kick he scored against Crystal Palace where he beat a six-man wall to curl the ball into the upper right-hand corner.

Unfortunately Payet's second season did not match the heights of the first and he eventually returned to Marseille in January 2017.

Forwards

Michu may be the Lionel Messi of one-season wonders.

When the Spaniard joined Swansea from Rayo Vallecano in July 2012, few could have foretold what was to come.



Michu scored twice and provided an assist on his debut for the Swans in what was very much a sign of things to come.

By the end of the campaign, Michu had 18 league goals to his name, with only Robin van Persie, Luis Suarez, Gareth Bale and Christian Benteke all scoring more.

6 Michu's first season at Swansea is fondly remembered by fans Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Jamie O'Hara and Jermaine Pennant's Premier League Cult Hero XI Goalkeeper: Gabor Kiraly Defenders: Nadir Belhadj, Neil Ruddock, Ivan Campo Midfielders: Thomas Gravesen, Park Ji-sung, Damien Duff, Dimitri Payet Forwards: Michu, Fabrizio Ravanelli, Nwankwo Kanu

Michu also inspired Swansea to League Cup glory, the club's first and only major trophy to date.



Sadly, the rest of Michu's career was derailed by injury and was forced to retire in 2017 aged 31.

Joining Michu in the striking department for the Cult Hero XI are Fabrizio Ravanelli and Nwankwo Kanu.

Ravanelli, nicknamed the 'White Feather', rocked up to Middlesbrough in the summer of 1996 after four seasons with Italian giants Juventus.

Even though he banged in 16 league goals for Boro, Ravanelli didn't exactly endear himself to the club or supporters.



He once claimed Boro's training facilities were 'not adequate' and that English players 'have a natural gift for running' but could not match the technical skills of Italian players.

Arsenal rolled the dice on Kanu in 1999, signing him from Inter Milan despite the striker learning years before he had a serious heart issue which threatened to force him into an early retirement.

But the Nigerian defied his health concerns to enjoy five-and-a-half fruitful years with the Gunners where he won two Premier League titles and two FA Cups.

'King Kanu' scored a total of 44 goals for Arsenal across 197 appearances, with his catalogue of strikes ranging from the sublime to the simply ridiculous.

Sports.title: Premier League club told to hijack Danny Welbeck transfer to Chelsea at 11th hour
Sports.content:
Premier League club told to hijack Danny Welbeck transfer to Chelsea at 11th hour

Manchester United have been urged to hijack Chelsea's move for Danny Welbeck.

The former England striker is set to join the Blues from Brighton on a two-year deal, talkSPORT understands.

3 United have been told to consider hijacking Chelsea's move for Welbeck Credit: AFP

Welbeck has been given permission to undergo a medical with Chelsea.

Personal terms have already been agreed with the 35-year-old, who is expected to join up with his new team-mates in Hong Kong as part of their pre-season tour.

However, Welbeck's former club United have been told they should attempt a last-minute hijack for the veteran forward.

The Red Devils academy graduate spent 13 years at the club before he was sold to Arsenal in 2014.

Welbeck to United?

Appearing on the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Devils, Angelina Kelly called for United to move for Welbeck.

Asked if Michael Carrick's side should hijack the deal, she exclaimed: "Yes, we 100 per cent should.

"I love Danny Welbeck. The Angelina Kelly household approves this message. We are a Welbeck household.

"This guy, there is nothing that could make me dislike Danny Welbeck. I just think he’s great.

"He’s a Manc lad. Even when he was at Arsenal, I wasn’t mad at him. I was like, ‘you go Danny Welbeck, you go and you have fun, you make something of yourself.’"

Having made his first-team debut aged 17, Welbeck went on to score 29 goals in 142 appearances for United.

3 Welbeck scored 29 goals in 142 appearances for boyhood club United Credit: AFP

Man United pre-season on MUTV Fans can watch Michael Carrick prepare for the new season and how the squad is shaping up across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Ireland. MUTV is the home of all Manchester United pre-season fixtures. It’s the opportunity to watch new faces, young players, returning names, tactical clues and the first signs of what United might become over the next season. MUTV on Sky: £7 extra a month. Existing Sky TV customers only. 31 day rolling contract. Cancel anytime with 31 days’ notice. Requires compatible Sky Q or Sky Stream boxes.

He also won eight trophies including two Premier League titles and the Champions League.

Ease the burden

The addition of a new striker would ease the burden on Benjamin Sesko ahead of his second season at Old Trafford.

Although Carrick also has Joshua Zirkzee and Matheus Cunha as centre-forward options, the 23-year-old is set to be his starting No.9.

Sesko scored 11 goals in 30 Premier League outings last term following his arrival from RB Leipzig.

Kelly continued: "I just think it would be a great option because Benjamin Sesko is the future with Manchester United.

"I think he had a really good season overall, when you consider everything that was going on. He’s come back, he looks very built in the upper body, he’s been in the gym.

3 Kelly believes signing Welbeck would ease the burden on Sesko at United next season Credit: Getty

Danny Welbeck's career statistics 2001-14: Manchester United - 29 goals in 142 appearances 2010: Preston North End (Loan) - Two goals in eight appearances 2010-11: Sunderland (Loan) - Six goals in 28 appearances 2014-19: Arsenal - 32 goals in 126 appearances 2019-20: Watford - Three goals in 20 appearances 2020-Present: Brighton - 51 goals in 201 appearances 2011-18: England - 16 goals in 42 caps Honours: Champions League, 2x Premier League, Club World Cup, 2x FA Cup, 2x League Cup, 3x Community Shield

"I don’t like the idea of having it all on his shoulders. We’ve seen that happen a couple of times with the Manchester United strikers.

"Yes, we’ve got younger players, somebody like Chido Obi [Martin], for example, who’s coming through. No guarantees with that.

"I think to have somebody like Welbeck, who knows the Premier League, knows Manchester United, I think he should have been in the World Cup squad, to be honest.

"I was sad that he didn’t get that call-up. That’s the level that he’s at. To have someone like him, be able to fill in if there are injuries, to be able to rotate because we’re hoping that Man United go far in the cup competitions. We can’t have another Grimsby situation. It cannot happen.

"I think that he’d be a great asset and I understand why Chelsea are going in for him. I think that especially with their discipline issues and all that stuff, I think he’d bring a lot of calm."

Welbeck missed out on a place in England's final World Cup squad despite scoring 13 league goals last season.

Those strikes took his Premier League tally to 90 in 400 appearances for Brighton, United, Arsenal, Sunderland and Watford.

Sports.title: Tottenham plot £60m raid for Premier League winger to take transfer spending over £250m
Sports.content:
Tottenham plot £60m raid for Premier League winger to take transfer spending over £250m

Tottenham have rekindled their interest in Man City winger Savinho after holding initial talks last summer.

The Brazil international has emerged as a key target for Roberto De Zerbi, with the player keen to depart in search of more first-team minutes.

3 Spurs have reportedly reignited their interest in Man City winger Savinho Credit: Getty

The process of securing the move to the capital is now underway after the attacker spent two years under Pep Guardiola.

The 22-year-old signed for City from sister club Troyes for £30million in July 2024, having spent the previous campaign on loan at Catalan side Girona.

Savinho had talks with the Lilywhites last year, but former Man City boss Guardiola blocked the negotiations.

The Brazilian subsequently signed a two-year contract extension in October, keeping him at the Etihad Stadium until 2031.

He was a regular starter in his first season, scoring three times in 48 appearances across all competitions.

However, during Guardiola's final season at the club, the winger's playing minutes were limited to only 14 starts across the full season in an injury-hit campaign.

Savinho faced intense competition for his position from Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

City wanted around £70m a year ago — and Spurs chiefs are now working on a deal worth closer to £60m.

On talkSPORT's White and Jordan, chief football correspondent Alex Crook stated: "I don’t think the interest from last summer and January has ever really gone away.

"It was Pep Guardiola who put the stoppers on that move this time a year ago and he had no kind of season at all at Manchester City.

"I think the player is keen to make the move and Roberto De Zerbi is keen to sign him. Around £60 million is the fee being touted, and this would be another addition to the Tottenham squad that De Zerbi is assembling."

The hierarchy at the north London club have backed the Italian manager in the transfer window following back-to-back 17th-place finishes.

Despite the attacker's desire to leave, he was included in Enzo Maresca's initial 28-man squad for their pre-season tour of Asia.

City will face Inter Milan, the K League All-Stars, and Atletico Madrid in Hong Kong and Seoul.

3 Maresca may be more open to selling Savinho Credit: AFP

Man City 28-man squad Goalkeepers: Marcus Bettinelli, Gianluigi Donnarumma, Max Chabot, Jack Wint. Defenders: Rayan Ait-Nouri, Max Alleyne, Kaden Braithwaite, Josko Gvardiol, Matty Henderson-Hall, Abdukodir Khusanov, Rico Lewis, Stephen Mfuni, Vitor Reis Midfielders: Claudio Echeverri, Phil Foden, Jaden Heskey, Mateo Kovacic, Jeremy Monga, Divine Mukasa, Nico, Xavier Parker, Tijjani Reijnders, Floyd Samba, Antoine Semenyo, Savinho. Forwards: Ryan McAidoo, Divin Mubama, Mahamadou Sangare

Spurs transfer spending

If Spurs were to pay the expected fee for Savinho, he would become the club's fourth-most expensive signing.

Spurs have already broken their transfer record fee twice this summer with Sandro Tonali (£100m), and Mateus Fernandes (£85m).

3 Tonali broke Spurs' transfer record by £35million Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

They also splashed out £52m for Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton to take their total spend to £237m so far.

Meanwhile, the north London side have acquired Marcos Senesi, Andy Robertson, and Martin Dubravka on free transfers.

Sports.title: Former EFL stadium left to rot for years could finally be demolished
Sports.content:
Former EFL stadium left to rot for years could finally be demolished

Rotherham United's former stadium could be demolished 18 years after the League Two club left the ground.

The Millers, who currently play in League Two, played home matches at Millmoor for 83 years before departing in 2008.



3 Millmoor, the former home of Rotherham, could be demolished 18 years after they left Credit: Getty

In the near two decades since, the 8,300-capacity ground has been left largely unused.

Whilst the pitch and goalposts remain intact, the stands and buildings have become increasingly run down.

Despite renovation work in 2024, Millmoor could now finally be torn down if plans are approved by the local council.



It is hoped permission will be given to demolish the Millmoor Lane and Railway stands as well as surrounding buildings.

The floodlights would also be removed under the proposed plans, which could be completed by January.



Uncertain future

Despite being opened in 1920, Millmoor was last renovated in 2004.

The ground had remained under the ownership of former Rotherham chief Ken Booth despite his exit from the club the same year.

With new owner Tony Stewart unable to agree a deal for the stadium, the Millers left their old home in 2008.



The Booth family later renovated Millmoor before it was briefly reopened to the public last year.

Both Doncaster Rovers Belles and local youth football matches were subsequently held at the venue.

3 Rotherham played home matches at Millmoor for 83 years before their final outing at the ground in 2008 Credit: Getty

However, CF Booth have since entered administration, with the Ron Hull Group acquiring Millmoor.



A statement released in May provided an update on the ground's future, explaining: "The buildings and structures selected in the current application to demolish are all in a poor condition due to years of neglect and are suffering from a general lack of maintenance, specifically elements like roof finishes and the structures themselves.

"It is assumed this situation accelerated in the period since Rotherham United Football Club vacated the site.

"The current main stand is only partially completed, and has been exposed to the elements since at least 2007.

"The high cost of repair, let alone to proceed to complete this stand would be excessive given that there are very limited numbers of possible users of the ground. Thus meaning it is unbuyable."



Rotherham's new home

Following their exit from Millmoor, Rotherham spent four years playing at Don Valley Stadium, an athletics ground in Sheffield.

3 Plans could be approved to demolish two stands, surrounding buildings and the floodlights at Millmoor Credit: Shutterstock

The club finally found a permanent home in 2012 following the construction of the New York Stadium, half a mile from their old home.

They have continued to play at the 12,021-capacity stadium for the last 14 years.



In that time, the club have experienced five promotions and five relegations.

However, last season saw the club drop into League Two for the first time since 2013 just two years on from playing Championship football.

Sports.title: UEFA hit out over Gianni Infantino's controversial plans to sell the World Cup - and appear to accuse FIFA of bribing associations to support new proposal
Sports.content:
UEFA have seemingly accused FIFA of bribing associations as they continue to scold Gianni Infantino's plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - criticising FIFA’s self-interest as they pressure associations with a £30million incentive.

FIFA wrote to national associations on Wednesday morning to explain their leaked plans, detailing that a £30m funding package will become available to associations should they sign off on the World Cup private investment plan.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says associations must decide on the proposal - which would see private investors procure a £3bn interest in the World Cup - by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

In response to the letter, UEFA said: 'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn. This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

Sources have told Daily Mail Sport that UEFA have scheduled crisis talks with all 55 member nations on Thursday as they rally the troops against FIFA.

Tensions have long been growing between FIFA President Gianni Infantino and UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin, who boycotted the World Cup final

FIFA hope to set up a company responsible for the commercial activity and 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

Sports.title: Liverpool prepare to submit opening bid for £145m-rated PSG winger Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool are set to table an opening offer for top target Bradley Barcola.

The Reds are preparing their first offer for the Paris Saint-Germain winger, who is valued at £145million.

They do not want to pay the French club’s asking price and hope a deal can be done for a smaller figure.

Barcola is understood to be keen to join Liverpool after the club held talks with his representatives in the last week.

The 23-year-old France international has indicated he does not wish to sign a new contract with the European champions and is open to joining Liverpool, who have a long-held interest.

PSG are considering his sale but he still has two years left on his contract and they believe, based on his age, potential and current market prices, that £145m is a fair price.

Liverpool are set to table an opening offer for PSG's £145milion-rated Bradley Barcola

Liverpool will seek a compromise on that with Barcola's price reputed to have been closer to £75million last summer when they first sounded out his representatives.

Barcola is not a regular starter for Luis Enrique's side and they have been pursuing RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande, which would have pushed him further down the pecking order, only for Real Madrid to declare their intent to sign the Ivory Coast international on Friday – which is now close to completion.

Liverpool also had an £85million proposal rejected for Diomande, but Barcola has always been in their thinking.

He has the skillset to suit Andoni Iraola's style and can provide a serious goal threat following the void left by Mohamed Salah's departure.

Across the past two seasons at PSG, Barcola scored 34 goals and assisted a further 28.

He played in all eight of France's World Cup matches this year, scoring three goals, including one against England in the third-place play-off.

Arsenal and Bayern Munich also retain interest in Barcola while Chelsea made enquiries earlier in the summer.

Sports.title: FIFA pile pressure on nations over Gianni Infantino's controversial proposal to sell the World Cup - with members given just 53 days to decide whether they accept £30m offer
Sports.content:
FIFA are attempting to pressure their 211 member associations into backing plans to sell stakes in the World Cup - just hours after the FA voiced deep concerns over Gianni Infantino's divisive proposals.

News broke on Tuesday that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion, which the governing body later confirmed in a hastily-issued statement.

In a letter to the associations, Infantino says member nations must decide on the proposal by September 19 and explains the financial benefits of approving the project.

He says that a funding package around £30million per nation will become available if associations sign up, but if they reject it their earnings will be almost 75 per cent less.

The letter from Infantino says: ‘The decision on whether or not to proceed with this proposal belongs entirely to you. Should you wish to proceed this $10billion package will become available as of January 1, 2027, ushering in the next phase of our journey together.

‘Should you wish to retain the status quo and reject this proposal we still have our planned expansion of the Forward programme [development money] of $2.7billion as previously presented.

‘In total for the upcoming cycle starting as of January 1, 2027 each member association will have the possibility of access up to $40million per member association under this proposal.’

UEFA have responded to the letter, insinuating that FIFA are attempting to bribe associations into accepting the proposition.

'Today we have learned of FIFA’s deadline to associations to support their proposals or have the one-off payout offer withdrawn,' UEFA said. 'This says everything you need to know about this plan.

'But having held discussions with many stakeholders across the game, UEFA knows there is significant and growing opposition to FIFA’s scheme. FIFA cannot continue to use our sport to enrich themselves and their friends. We can grow the game correctly. It’s time to prioritise associations, clubs, leagues, players and fans.'

The FA have deep concerns over FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup

Investment bank J.P. Morgan is FIFA's financial advisor on the project while Joshua Kushner's Thrive Capital is expected to lead the proposed investor group. Kushner is the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared. The Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

FIFA hope to raise more than £3bn for the venture from a diversified, global investor group which is thought to include sovereign wealth funds.

Should their plans be successful, FIFA intend to give each of their 211 member associations a stake in the company - which they can choose to keep or sell - worth £15m.

The FA, though, are worried about FIFA's leaked plans to sell stakes in the World Cup.

In a statement, an FA spokesperson confirmed they had been left in the dark over the controversial proposals which have sparked outrage amongst the football community.

The statement said: 'We were completely unaware of this proposal and have no substantive details, including what the proposition actually is, and what conditions are attached.

'Based on the limited information, we are deeply concerned about the lack of process and governance to get to this point, and the apparent substance and principles involved.

'When the proposal is shared in the full and transparent way now promised by FIFA, we will make our views clear, and comment further.'

It has been suggested that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, although FIFA claim that has not been discussed.

European Football Clubs, who represent over 800 European clubs, have voiced their opposition. Crucially, the body is chaired by PSG President Nasser Al-Khelaifi and Qatar Sports Investments, who are owned by the Qatari state. Al-Khelaifi has been touted as a potential leadership challenger to Infantino.

'European Football Clubs (EFC) notes with serious concern the sudden, unilateral media briefings and announcement by FIFA about a potential new corporate structure for the commercialisation of certain football competitions,' the statement read.

'As an institution that represents over 850 football clubs – whose member clubs, their players and communities are fundamental participants in football worldwide, not least in FIFA’s competitions including all the international club competitions – it would be wholly appropriate for EFC to be fully consulted on a proposal of such magnitude. EFC learned about this proposal in the same way as most global football stakeholders – without warning and through the media.

'EFC always seeks to work collaboratively and supportively with all stakeholders – FIFA, UEFA and all confederations, national associations, leagues, player and fan associations.

'In that vein, we urge for calm and thorough consultation on all topics affecting the football ecosystem, together with more rigorous and transparent governance processes put in place to protect the game for the long term. Only in this way can we build the right institutional frameworks and relationships required to promote the true success, stability and sustainability of football.'

Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also among the dissenting voices.

'Let me say this very directly,' Burnham posted on X. 'Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

One European nation has already publicly supported Infantino's plan, with the President of the Czech FA David Trunda backing him.

'I can see the pragmatic benefits for Czech football from working in close co-operation with [FIFA president] Gianni Infantino and his team,' Trunda told Sky News.

"Of course we need more details, but my personal point of view is that I can see the positive impact of FIFA's intentions."

FIFA want to set up a new company responsible for the 'operational delivery of FIFA tournaments', called FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE).

They claim the plans would help advance the FIFA Forward development programme, which distributes capital to member associations. The governing body hopes to increase funding from £6m to £15m for the 2027-30 international cycle.

FIFA would need approval from the FIFA Council and majority support from the FIFA Congress (the 211 member associations) to launch the new enterprise.

Three of the six continental confederations have expressed resistance, including UEFA who released a scathing statement on Tuesday.

'This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross," UEFA said. UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell.'

CONCACAF, the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean, added: 'CONCACAF was only made aware of this matter through media reports and, subsequently, via a media release,' their statement read on Wednesday morning.

'We are deeply concerned by the lack of due process.

'We share the disappointment of many within our region and the game that this level of detail has been designed and shared publicly before any discussion with the relevant governance bodies and stakeholders has taken place.

'As leaders within football, we are the custodians of the game. Collectively, FIFA, the Confederations and every Member Association have a responsibility to always act in the best interests of the sport. Every decision we make must be guided by good governance, robust processes and long-term stewardship.

'This is the framework within which Concacaf operates. We trust that all within the FIFA family will act in the same manner.'

The Asian federation have also stated their disappointment at the lack of consultation from FIFA.

There are major concerns over what the proposals could mean for the game, including whether FIFA could increase the frequency of tournaments to create more opportunities for financial backers to see a return on their investment.

The Club World Cup and men's World Cup are currently held every four years. FIFA have previously explored the possibility of staging both tournaments every two years.

FIFA maintain that they have a duty to control the development of this project, with external investors holding only a minority stake in FFE and having no operational role.

Sports.title: Turkey's bid to be a football giant: Why Mohamed Salah would be a 'BURDEN' to Besiktas, Galatasaray's private island, how clubs have lost almost £500M in four years - and the restaurant serving ribs coated in gold
Sports.content:
Victor Osimhen had a decision to make. It was September 2024 and prospective moves to Al-Ahli and Chelsea had fallen through at the 11th hour. Napoli had kicked him out of the squad and replaced him with Romelu Lukaku. A bleak season awaited.

Then came the call from Galatasaray manager Okan Buruk. Why not come to Turkey?

'As a father, I want you at my club,' said Buruk, a man nicknamed 'The Winner One' – you can ask Jose Mourinho why. 'These fans will love you. They will do everything for you.'

So Osimhen, one of Europe's most coveted strikers and then only 25, took the plunge and moved to a league which has never quite gatecrashed the elite. He landed at 3am on September 3 and, true to Buruk's word, the fans loved him. Three thousand were there to welcome him with flares, despite a flight delay of several hours.

In July last year, he signed permanently for a Turkish transfer record of £64.1million. As he puts it, he has found his 'love story'.

This is the treatment which awaits Mohamed Salah, if indeed he finalises a move to Besiktas, one of Turkish football's 'big three' in Istanbul alongside Galatasaray and Fenerbahce. Talks have stalled but the reported wage on offer is £10.7m per year, plus a heap of add-ons. There is, it seems, a hitch over the shirt sales revenue Salah will be entitled to, as well as the commission his camp will get. His alternative destinations would likely be in Saudi Arabia and the United States.

Mohamed Salah could be on the move to Besiktas - but experts warn his financial demands would be a huge 'burden' for the Turkish club

The lifestyle is a huge appeal; Former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson is seen on a cruise down the Bosphorus Strait

Salt Bae's Nusr-Et restaurant attracts the top stars - Lionel Messi and Paul Pogba once went there together

The Nusr-Et restaurant will even coat your meat in gold for a premium price

Besiktas' fans have limited patience. During Leandro Trossard's recent unveiling, they chanted Salah's name instead. But Ahmet Turgut, host of the Turkish Football Podcast, feels they should be careful what they wish for.

'The price is too much - it would hurt Besiktas. They would sell a lot of shirts and have fans greeting him in the beginning, but if he had a season like he did at Liverpool, these fans would boo Salah,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It would be a burden on Besiktas. Already they are financially in trouble.

'The clubs in general are not managed by professionals. It’s not like in England and Europe who have owners and a professional team under them. Every year, all three of them want to be champions and that is causing them financial problems.

‘These three clubs need to look in the mirror and change their habit of transferring all these players and the money going down the drain wasted.'

It is an increasingly frequent tale, marquee names going to Turkey – and not just for teeth and hair transplants. In the past four years, Turkish clubs have made a net loss of £444.51million, a figure exceeded only by the Premier League, Saudi Pro League, and Serie A.

Osimhen's weekly salary of around £300,000 is only bettered in the Premier League by Erling Haaland and Virgil van Dijk. Ederson, N'Golo Kante, Leroy Sane, Ilkay Gundogan, Leandro Trossard, and Mason Greenwood all call Istanbul home now. AC Milan's Rafael Leao, who is 27 and has had interest from Real Madrid, Liverpool, and both Manchester clubs, looks more likely to join... Fenerbahce.

How are Turkey's top teams pulling this off? The attraction is that the league lives in a sweet spot: rich but not as brazenly so as the Gulf states, fiercely competitive, and with huge lifestyle benefits.

'For Salah, if he goes to Besiktas, a large part of the decision will be that he wants to do something special and write a nice last chapter to his career. If you go to Saudi, everyone knows you're there to cash in. You're not adding much value to your story,' Kaan Bayazit, host of the Black Eagles podcast about Besiktas, tells Daily Mail Sport.

Players are treated like kings in Turkey and lavishly paid - Victor Osimhen earns more than £300,000 per week at Galatasaray

Galatasaray have invested in part of a private island for their players to enjoy time in peace

Ex-Man City man Nathan Ake plays for Fenerbahce and enjoys time with his wife Kaylee

'In Turkey, you have the potential to play in the Champions League and are playing in a top-10 European league. You have some of the biggest derbies in the world. There's a lot to like for a footballer.

'Istanbul is an even bigger city than London. There's so much luxury, hotels, dining opportunities. It's a great place for footballers to live - but you can't go to the supermarket without getting mobbed.'

Bayazit also sends a warning: 'The passion of the fans can definitely be a negative. If Salah goes to Turkey and doesn't do well, and he's spurning 12 million euros a year, then fans will turn toxic for sure. It's not likely, but it happened to Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain.'

Oxlade-Chamberlain spent two years at Besiktas but struggled to find his best form. He played under eight managers and four club presidents, and when things went south, fans turned up at the training ground to share their unsavoury thoughts.

The lavish spending is yet to translate to enhanced performances in Europe. In the 21st century, Turkish clubs have only made it out of the Champions League group stages four times – and the last to reach the quarter-finals was Galatasaray in 2001. Besiktas were the most recent Turkish club to reach the Europa League quarters in 2016-17. Fenerbahce once reached the last eight of the Conference League.

It is an abysmal record given their potential and it would be easy to say, therefore, that the money is the main draw. But the players themselves appear equally taken in by the special treatment they receive, as well as the sheer fervour of the fanbases.

As Sane jetted in last summer, then aged 29, Galatasaray's live stream of his arrival in the city reached a peak audience of 3.2 million viewers. Thousands of supporters greeted him at the airport. His image was projected onto the 14th-century Galata Tower – and he wasn't even officially their player yet.

When Jose Mourinho was at Fenerbahce, they put him up in the luxurious Four Seasons hotel for 16 months and racked up a £656,000 bill. His accommodation, one of the finest hotels in the city, boasted a spa, state-of-the-art gym and indoor and outdoor swimming pools. Each day, a chauffeur drove him to and from Fenerbahce's Can Bartu training complex, and when he was back home, he would allegedly always have the same meal: chicken soup followed by margherita pizza, ice cream and sparkling water.

Players are given a heroes' welcome when they arrive in Istanbul to sign for a 'big three' club

Leroy Sane's face was projected onto the historic Galata Tower ahead of his Galatasaray move

Matteo Guendouzi and his wife Maelle moved toIstanbul during the last transfer window

Former Arsenal star Matteo Guendouzi has been at Fenerbahce with his wife Maelle and their two daughters since January. They share a lavish house on a hilltop with a swimming pool overlooking the rooftops and, in their quality time together, take romantic boat trips down the Bosphorus through the heart of the city.

Istanbul has thousands of restaurants to choose from – one travel blog estimates around 23,000 – with Salt Bae's original Nusr-Et restaurant in the Besiktas district, a popular haunt among footballers. Lionel Messi and Paul Pogba once met there for Turkish tea – but diners can also order ribs coated in 24-carat gold for the equivalent of more than £300.

Salt Bae – whose real name is Nusret Gokce – is a lifelong fan of Fenerbahce and has a strong connection with the club, having hosted players for meals and joined in with their basketball team's title celebrations on-court.

There is a concerted effort from Turkey's elite teams to build an environment which can host the very best. Galatasaray moved into a new 130-acre training facility last year which cost around £17.5m, alongside spending on upgrading their academy and other sports branches. They have also invested in a private island in the middle of the Bosphorus Strait and turned it into an exclusive destination where players can enjoy parties and fine dining.

Besiktas moved into a fresh £86m stadium a decade ago and are planning to build a new training ground near Istanbul Airport. They are currently saddled with debts of around £387m, as per their latest announcement, but hope to erase that via investment in a state-backed real estate project.

There is a feeling at Besiktas and Fenerbahce that they must play catch-up to Galatasaray, who have brought in enormous revenues from four consecutive title wins and Champions League campaigns each season.

For Turgut, the race is a treacherous one and points to a fundamental problem in how the big three are run.

He said: 'They have elections with the members voting every two years. If you buy the members, you’ll be president. This system has to change, otherwise it will be the same thing with other clubs. We’ll see the clubs go bankrupt or they’ll get bought by some people.'

Maybe all the stellar names and lavish spending can propel them into the continental elite and bring them financial rewards unlike ever before, though?

Not so for Turgut: ‘I don’t see any hope for Turkish teams doing really well in European competitions in the future.’

Sports.title: Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future - plus, the latest on Tottenham star Manor Solomon as West Ham circle: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Man City push for World Cup wonderkid

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The teenage Morocco international is ready to make the move now though Lille would prefer him to stay for another season.

City would want Bouaddi for this season with Real Madrid ready to push for Rodri who is keen to return to Spain for family reasons.

Though they have added Elliot Anderson, they have lost Bernardo Silva and could also sell Nico Gonzalez and Tijjani Reijnders who has interest from Galatasaray and earlier in the summer Atletico Madrid.

The 18-year-old Bouaddi has plenty of admirers but City are ready to meet the terms required to prise him away.

Manchester City and Lille are holding further negotiations over the proposed £80million transfer of midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, who impressed for Morocco at the World Cup

Henderson exit paves way for Chelsea move

Brentford have announced that Jordan Henderson has left the club by mutual consent.

The 36-year-old has held talks with Xabi Alonso ahead of joining Chelsea.

As Daily Mail Sport reported, Brentford are working to sign Mamadou Sangare from Lens and have interest in Pape Sarr from Spurs.

Potters star attracting attention

Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry City, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa.

The Wales international impressed against Everton in Stoke’s 1-0 friendly win on Tuesday evening and interest has been building in the 27-year-old following his last campaign where he scored ten goals in the Championship.

Stoke are understood to value him around £9million.

Stoke star Sorba Thomas is attracting interest from Coventry, West Ham, Stuttgart and Genoa

Boro ask about in-demand Travers

Middlesbrough have made enquiries for Everton goalkeeper Mark Travers over a permanent transfer.

The Republic of Ireland, who started in Everton's friendly defeat to Stoke on Tuesday night, has been the subject of a number of enquiries this summer including from Coventry who finally agreed a £22.5million fee plus add ons with Brighton for Carl Rushworth on Tuesday.

Iliman Ndiaye is subject to interest from Saudi side Al Hilal this summer

Boro have also asked about Manchester United's Radek Vitek but 27-year-old Travers has been at the club before on loan and could prove cheaper. He joined Everton from Bournemouth last year in a four-year deal.

Meanwhile, Everton have still to receive an offer from Al Hilal for Iliman Ndiaye. They are aware of interest but have no desire to sell, though the 26-year-old has turned down offers of a new contract.

Koleosho heads to Paris

Burnley winger Luca Koleosho has completed a permanent move to Ligue 1 side Paris FC for an undisclosed fee.

Clyne flies the Eagles nest again

Crystal Palace have confirmed that Nathaniel Clyne has left the club following the expiration of his contract.

The full back, who made 252 appearances across two stints at Selhurst Park, told Palace TV: 'The last few seasons have given me some of the best days of my life.

'When I started at Crystal Palace we were in the Championship. Now the club is playing European football, having nights like we did in Leipzig.'

Palace remain in talks over a possible permanent deal for Takehiro Tomiyasu, who is training with the club in Como. Discussions are also continuing over defensive targets Chrislain Matsima and Raphael Le Guen.

Takehiro Tomiyasu is currently training with Crystal Palace as he seeks to find a new club

Bees hoping to seal Sangare deal

Lens are looking at Lorient's Arthur Avom Ebong and Melayro Bogarde from LASK as potential replacements for Brentford target Mamadou Sangare.

Brentford are discussing a £40million deal for Sangare, as reported by Daily Mail Sport, and hope to finalise terms quickly ahead of competition from the likes of Crystal Palace for the 24-year-old, who was named in the Ligue 1 Team of the Year last season.

Brentford are long-term admirers of the player and signing a new central midfielder was a priority even before Chelsea moved for Jordan Henderson. They also like Spurs' Pape Matar Sarr.

City teen heads to Leicester

Manchester City left back Christian McFarlane has joined Leicester on loan.

McFarlane, 19, becomes the third signing through the door at the King Power Stadium this summer. He joins Conor Chaplin and Alex McCarthy in bolstering Russell Martin's squad.

New Leicester boss Russell Martin has bolstered his team's promotion bid with the signing of Man City left back Christian McFarlane

McFarlane said: 'As a player, I’m intense and aggressive at both ends – attacking and defending. I like to make runs in behind and can be a bit of a nuisance for the opposition.

'The way [the manager] wants to play suits me perfectly, so I’m excited to get started.'

Blues close to landing Lund

Birmingham are closing on a deal for Palermo left back Kristoffer Lund.

The 24-year-old Dane spent last season on loan at Cologne but the German side did not take up their £2.5m option to buy.

Solomon set on permanent switch

Manor Solomon wants to leave Tottenham on a permanent transfer amid interest from West Ham.

The Israeli winger’s agent has made it clear he does not wish for another loan move, after spells with Leeds, Villarreal and Fiorentina, and that’s expected to suit Spurs as they look to recoup funds and upgrade their wide options.

Meanwhile, Spurs are closing on agreement with Wolves for Kwasi Senyah. The 16-year-old defensive midfielder and England youth international was wanted by several clubs but will join Spurs once terms are agreed and it is cleared by the FA.

Benfica are showing interest in Spurs left wing-back Souza while Leicester remain hopeful of taking 18-year-old centre back prospect Malachi Hardy.

Manor Solomon's Tottenham career has struggled to take-off since his move from Shakhtar Donetsk

Rovers return for Vaulks

Wales international Will Vaulks is in talks over a move to Tranmere.

The 32-year-old started his career with the Wirral club but never made a senior appearance.

Vaulks has gone on to play nearly 600 games at Sheffield Wednesday, Cardiff and Rotherham before arriving at Oxford United. He made 38 appearances in the Championship for them last season but is now looking to return home.

Tranmere have also snapped up goalkeeper Harrison Male on a one-year contract. The 25-year-old was a free transfer after he was released by York City earlier this summer.

He played 46 games as the Minstermen pipped Rochdale to the National League title and won Golden Glove after keeping 19 clean sheets.

Click below for all the transfer developments over the last few days...

Tuesday: Man United open to offer for four academy graduates

MONDAY: Leeds close in on deal for James Trafford

SUNDAY: Liverpool seek compromise on Bradley Barcola

SATURDAY: Tottenham continue push for Man City winger Savinho

FRIDAY: Real open talks for Yan Diomande, Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee... and Brentford bid for West Ham wing back

THURSDAY: Arsenal sign Christos Tzolis in £34million move from Club Brugge as Leeds ramp up talks with Man City's James Trafford

WEDNESDAY: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal

Sports.title: Pochettino makes decision on USA future after World Cup ended in disaster
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino is close to agreeing an extension to remain as head coach of the USMNT through to the 2030 World Cup, despite their campaign ending in disaster.

The 54-year-old's initial contract expired following the World Cup, where the USMNT suffered a dispiriting 4-1 thrashing at the hands of Belgium in the round of 16.

However, US Soccer and Pochettino are now closing in on a new four-year deal that will keep the Argentine at the helm through to 2030, according to The Athletic.

Talks between the two parties were initially paused during the tournament, but negotiations have progressed rapidly following discussions between the two parties.

'Right now, it's about resting a little, to think, have conversations with the federation to see what the decision is. I'm so happy,' Pochettino said following the Belgium loss.

Meanwhile, US Soccer CEO JT Batson also confirmed that active discussions were underway regarding the future of the program's coaching staff.

Mauricio Pochettino is set to sign a contract extension with the USA that will run until 2030

The USA crashed out of the World Cup with a humiliating 4-1 defeat to Belgium in the last 16

'From a men's national team coaching standpoint, we're in active discussions with Mauricio and staff about the future,' Batson explained.

'We all share a belief that the best days of US Soccer are ahead of us'.

While the manner of their World Cup exit raised questions over Pochettino's lucrative salary, the USMNT enjoyed a strong stage performance under his tenure - securing first place in their group after winning their opening two matches of the tournament.

Pochettino, who took charge of the national team in October 2024, has remained actively involved in the federation's long-term planning since taking the reins.

However, not everyone shares the federation's faith in the manager. Fullback-turned-commentator Alexi Lalas claimed earlier this month that US Soccer should cut ties with Pochettino.

'I mean, it's not that I want him to leave,' the divisive 56-year-old told talkSPORT in the wake of the USA's World Cup exit . 'I just think that this cycle has run its course.'

'When it comes to Mauricio Pochettino, you had one job,' Lalas continued. 'And it was the game against Belgium. You win that game, then you're in some rarefied air. And it's not gravy but let's be honest, you're playing against Spain. And you take your chances, you're back in an underdog type of role.

'So I think that they [US Soccer] move on. I believe he's had a good time, but you had one job, and you blew it. And, you know, you live and die by that. Every coach understands that, every manager understands that, and certainly Mauricio Pochettino does.

The Argentine said that he would take a break before making a decision after the World Cup

'It was an abject failure,' Lalas continued. 'It's one thing to go out to Belgium, it's another thing to go out in the way they went out, especially with the way that they looked through the tournament.

'I don't think the confidence and excitement was misplaced for this team, but they picked the worst possible day to play their worst possible game. It's obviously on Mauricio Pochettino and these players.

'Does it completely negate everything they did? No. But the reality is a lot of that goodwill and a lot of the people that came into the tent … they're left shaking their head and there's an inquiry going on right now … rightfully holding this team and this coach to account.'

Pochettino was well received when he was named the USMNT head coach two years ago after previously coaching Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, and Chelsea.

There had been reports linking him to the AC Milan job, but the Italian giant has since hired ex-Manchester United manager Ruben Amorim.

Sports.title: Cricket scandal takes new twist as the club in cheating storm forfeit tonight's match with 'Clicky Ponting' cricketer 'knocked sideways' by global outrage
Sports.content:
Cricket scandal takes new twist as the club in cheating storm forfeit tonight's match with 'Clicky Ponting' cricketer 'knocked sideways' by global outrage

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The amateur cricket team at the centre of the 'Clicky Ponting' cheating scandal have been dumped out of a cup competition on Wednesday - after they conceded their forthcoming match.

Saltburn second Xl had been expected to take on Marton seconds on Wednesday evening in a 100-balls-a-side match.

But with backlash from the cheating row showing no sign of abating, Saltburn forfeited the game and will lose their place in the competition run by the North Yorkshire and South Durham League.

Saltburn fielder Brian Devine is accused of clicking his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball hitting the bat, to fool the umpire into thinking the batsman is out.

The amateur cricket scandal has caused convulsions around the cricketing world.

A source close to the league said: 'None of the Saltburn players will have wanted anything to do with this game while they're under such focus.

Saltburn Cricket Club have forfeited a cup match in light of the ongoing backlash against them

Brian Devine has been dubbed 'Clicky Ponting' on social media for his cricket fielding actions

Amateur cricket player Devine has been caught appearing to click his fingers to make it appear that a batter has been caught behind when in fact they haven't hit the ball at all

Saltburn player has been caught on camera clicking his fingers whenever ball was near bat

'They conceded the game and it won't be replayed which will mean they will effectively be knocked out of the cup as a result of what happened at the weekend.

'The match would have been a 100-ball thrash with the winner progressing to the later stages but Marton will go through now and Saltburn are out.

'For the lads that take their cricket seriously at Saltburn, that's a real blow but there was no way they were going to put themselves through that. It feels like the eyes of the world are on them right now.

'They are due to play Marton again on Saturday in a league match. It remains to be seen what happens there.'

The minor league cricketer at the centre of the Clicky Ponting cheating scandal is 'completely bewildered' to find himself engulfed by a global furore.

Friends say Brian Devine's 'head is all over the place' after the accusation that he clicked his fingers to imitate the sound of the ball snicking the bat in order to get opposing players dismissed.

Devine is expected to be dropped as his team, Saltburn Second Xl, was preparing for their first fixture since the cheating row erupted after their match with Norton seconds on Saturday in the North Yorkshire and South Durham cricket league.

Saltburn will take on Marton Seconds in a 100 balls-a-side league game on Wednesday night at Marton's ground in Middlesbrough.

Other incidences have been found of Devine clicking his finger in previous matches for wickets

A friend of Devine's said he was not expected to play and would 'lie low' while the cheating row continues.

The friend said: 'Brian is completely bewildered by the way this has gone all around the world.

'He's had an Australian podcast offering to pay his legal bills today - it's the first that he's heard that he's got any legal bills and he's hoping it won't get that far.

'His mates have been telling him to sell his story in Australia, but he just wants it all to go away and hopes he can get back to playing cricket, though at the moment that feels impossible for him.

'He woke up on Monday morning thinking the world was still the same place he'd left it the night before and suddenly his story was all over the world, in Australia, India, New Zealand and the UK of course.

'He understands why there is an investigation but the reaction all over the world to all this has knocked him sideways.'

Mr Devine, 38, a father who lives with his partner in Guisborough, North Yorks, continued to decline to comment on Wednesday. His mobile phone number was also removed from the company website at the auction mart in Northallerton where he works.

Saltburn Cricket Club are also yet to issue any kind of statement about the cheating allegations.

At the North Yorkshire seaside team's clubhouse, journalists were angrily told to leave by a club official, who said: 'We're sick of this now, you have no right to come here.'

Saltburn have been widely condemned on social media following multiple videos emerging

The furore erupted after Norton batter Noman Shabir insisted he hadn't touched the ball after was caught behind by the wicketkeeper and protested the decision to dismiss him.

Video footage shot from the sidelines appeared to show slip field Devine clicking his fingers at the moment the ball passed the bat.

Shabir explained what happened, posting online: 'We'd just lost a couple of quick wickets so I wanted to just see the ball first.

'Maybe if I went for a slog from the first ball and connected, I wouldn't have been "clicked" out. Sad thing is we can see from all the evidence in this thread that he's done it to all of the clubs in pretty much every game, and not a surprise now that they're currently sitting top of the table.

'Interestingly, when he got found out and the clicking stopped, the wickets also stopped for a long time and it became "boring" cricket for them.

'First ever time I've been "clicked" out in all the years I've been playing cricket, and clearly I'm not the only one.'

Norton Cricket Club declined to comment but directed enquiries to the league, who later said they were investigating.

Other teams have also raised questions, querying whether their players were fairly dismissed.

They point out that Saltburn's wicketkeeper Josh Bowes has taken 34 catches this season, close to double the record of his nearest counterpart, who has 19.

Norton batsman Noman Shabir protested that he didn't touch the ball after being given out

The skipper of another team in the same league said: 'It's now completely clear what has been happening and it was not confined to just one game.

'I was at the other end when one of our players was dismissed and I heard a big sound as the ball went through and immediately thought: "He's out."

'The umpire didn't hesitate either, but our batsman was adamant he was nowhere near the ball and couldn't understand the loud click.

'In all we had three batsmen given out who were caught behind but all of them said they didn't touch the ball. One protested so much the umpire had to have a word and threaten a warning.

'I know of at least three other teams who now have suspicions and it should be noted that in one match against Shildon their wicketkeeper took eight catches.

'You hear of all kinds of things going on in cricket but this is something I haven't heard of before and it's disgraceful that something like this has been happening in competitive cricket. I hope the league takes appropriate action.'

Sports.title: Roberto De Zerbi offers Lucas Bergvall ultimatum after surprise pre-season appearance as Tottenham stars made to work despite 30-hour trip: Tottenham 1-1 Sydney FC (4-2 on pens) TAKEAWAYS
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi has told Lucas Bergvall he would like him to stay with Tottenham – but insisted he will not beg the 20-year-old midfielder or promise him a place in his starting line-up.

Bergvall started in Spurs’ 1-1 friendly draw with Sydney FC in Australia before being replaced at half-time. The Sweden international is admired by Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, among others, and has now held talks with his manager about his situation.

De Zerbi spoke highly of Bergvall’s potential with reporters in Sydney, though told us how no elite club should ever need to try to convince a player to stay.

‘I would like that he stays with us,’ De Zerbi said of Bergvall. ‘I think he’s potentially a top, top, top player. But then I don’t want to convince anyone to stay. Tottenham is already, without me, a top club and we are not to convince anyone to stay. He can find the space if he stays with us.

‘The competition within the players will be very strong because we are Tottenham and we have to build a strong squad – not just 11 players, especially considering a lot of injuries we suffered in the last two, three seasons. Football is going in a clear direction.

'To compete for the highest places in the table, you have to manage 22, 23, 24 players. I don’t want 24, but 21, 22, of a high level, for sure. I was speaking with him before the end of the last season, and during the World Cup two times, but now we are speaking better, face to face, without a competition in this moment.

‘Now I started to work. In the last season we prepared the game, we worked in the head, on the mentality, more than the style of play. His position is very clear for me now. I needed time to understand the characteristics of the players. But I would like that he stays with us. He’s very young, a very good player, a good guy. It’s not so easy so fast to find a young player of that level.’

Lucas Bergvall started for Tottenham against Sydney - despite the midfielder wanting to leave

De Zerbi did mention there is room for improvement with Bergvall as he continued: ‘It’s very clear, his idea. He wants space (in the team). He wants to play as a double pivot as a position. I can’t give, for any player in the world, the place in the first XI guaranteed. Especially for me.

‘I want to be honest with the players. I want to be clear. I don’t want to make the first mistake. In terms of position, I can’t give guarantee. It’s right when he wants to play as a central midfielder.

‘But to play as a central midfielder, sometimes it is to attack, sometimes to keep the holder, to move the ball faster. He has to improve. He’s a 2006. I would like that he stays.

'But if he doesn’t want, then what can I do? Nothing. He has to speak with Vinai (Venkatesham, chief executive) or Johan Lange (sporting director). To stay with us, we have to have the right spirit to stay. He’s a good guy. We will see in the next weeks.’

Much like when Chelsea started Liam Delap against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday, Bergvall starting would suggest no move is immediately imminent, otherwise he would not have been risked. He was handed 45 minutes before being replaced.

While we must wait to see what happens with Bergvall, Spurs are not done trying to add to their squad this summer, despite their ambitious spending spree. They are now focusing on attackers in particular, and could indeed do with adding goals.

Spurs starlets spot-on

This friendly finishing 1-1 meant we had a penalty shootout to decide the winner of this Sydney Super Cup clash. Martin Dubravka and his goalkeeping coach took it serious enough to run through some instructions before the big showdown.

Spurs' scorers were Luca Williams-Barnett, the 17-year-old graduate who chose a cheeky Panenka, delicate as you like, straight down the middle. He had been shooting for fun during this match as if desperate to grab a goal, and so was allowed to step up first.

From there, Tonali, Andy Robertson and Dane Scarlett likewise scored for a 4-2 shootout win.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored a lovely Panenka penalty as Tottenham won 4-2 in the shootout

Robertson's steady debut

Robertson received the captain's armband when the 32-year-old Scot came on for his first pre-season minutes, and Spurs' new left back should have secured his first assist for the club.

Two of them, in fact. Min-Hyeok Yang was twice on the receiving end of crosses from Robertson – and twice the 20-year-old attacker failed to send the ball into the back of the net.

When Yang later failed to cross at the end of one flowing move, De Zerbi was jumping up and down on the spot in his technical area in frustration. The South Korea international has had three loans to Championship clubs since signing for Spurs upon turning 18 in January 2025.

Robertson continued to fly down the left flank in a highly attacking role, and only the fingertips of Sydney goalkeeper Gus Hoefsloot denied him a late winner here at the Allianz Stadium.

Andy Robertson made his first Spurs outing since joining and put in some good deliveries

Injury worry for one player

De Zerbi selected a young starting line-up for Sunday's 2-0 win over Auckland FC in New Zealand, resting his senior stars aside from Archie Gray. That was partially due to their 30 hours of travelling from the other side of the world, and following a few training sessions which have been described as gruelling under this demanding coach.

But a few of their first-teamers were back for this friendly versus Sydney FC, including Richarlison and Mathys Tel. However, when Manor Solomon was substituted, he was spotted with a pack of ice on his left thigh.

Manor Solomon had to have a pack of ice on his left thigh in a worrying concern for Tottenham

Rivalry resumed Down Under

There was a little awkwardness earlier this week when Tottenham and Chelsea sent representatives to an event on the Sydney shoreline to tee up this Australian tour. Spurs sent De Zerbi and Micky van de Ven, while the Blues sent Xabi Alonso and Robert Sanchez.

That saw De Zerbi briefly reunited with Sanchez, his former goalkeeper from Brighton who he essentially demoted before he left to join Chelsea. Not the nicest reunion, then, and Spurs will face Chelsea this Saturday in a friendly before they both leave Australia.

Sports.title: Amy Hunt proud after claiming Commonwealth 100m silver at sodden Scotstoun
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt proud after claiming Commonwealth 100m silver at sodden Scotstoun

Glass-half-full Amy Hunt splashed and sploshed her way to a 100m Commonwealth Games medal in drenched Glasgow last night

View Image Hunt added a Commonwealth Games silver medal to her collection of medals at World and Olympic level (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Relentlessly optimistic Amy Hunt has always been a glass-half-full personality. Hunt, who won world 200m silver last year, was looking to become the first British woman to win the Commonwealth 100m title in 40 years. Instead, a sluggish start meant she splished, splashed and sploshed to another silver medal at a sodden Scotstoun.

‌



However, the top-end speed she showed after stuttering from the blocks should give her confidence ahead of the European Championships in Birmingham next month, where, on this evidence, she'll be tough to beat in the 200m – surely a gilt-edged opportunity to win her first major individual title. The 24-year-old refused to blame the weather after clocking 10.98 seconds, just one hundredth outside her personal best despite the foul conditions.

‌



However, there will surely be a twinge of regret because this was a gold medal there for the taking, with Hunt having beaten the new champion, New Zealand's Zoe Hobbs, in the semi-finals. "My first 60 metres was really, really terrible, so I'm proud of how I dug myself out of a hole there," said Hunt.

‌



"It was pretty gross on the start – my fingers were underwater, which was a bit novel – but you have to roll with the punches at championships. I think some people would just say, 'Well, she's not a good starter,' but I think I've proven indoors that I'm a legitimate starter. I can get it right. Had I managed to execute a lot better in the first half, it might have been a different story.

"I got it really, really badly wrong, but my top-end speed is so formidable, and that's how I clawed back that silver. It was frustrating in the immediate aftermath, but having a medal is something you can't really describe. It's so intangible and almost ineffable. It's an amazing feeling to bring home that silver.

"I've now got every senior major championship covered with a medal, whether that's in the relay or individually, so I'm really, really proud of those achievements."

‌



In the last week, seven British Olympic medallists have withdrawn from these Games for a variety of reasons, though most are simply prioritising the Europeans over the Commonwealths. In contrast, Hunt likes a busy schedule. Her 2025 breakthrough season featured a full indoor campaign followed by an extensive, globe-trotting Diamond League programme. She won't compete in the 200m here but does expect to line up in England's sprint relay quartet.

Tiktok embed co"It's really important in terms of my journey as an athlete and my legacy as an athlete," she added. I don't want to go on my Wikipedia page in 30 years' time and just see one or two medals. I want to see lots of medals. That's really important to me.

"We don't get much representation in terms of media. We're not NBA players who are on TV three times a week and everyone's seeing our faces." Cameroon's Emmanuel Eseme claimed the men's 100m in a new Games record, adding the Commonwealth crown to his African title.

‌



Despite the teeming rain, he clocked a personal best 9.83 seconds to hold off Australia's Lachlan Kennedy by a fraction, as Nigeria's Kayinsola Ajayi completed the podium. Welsh sprinter Jeremiah Azu was the only Brit to reach the final, finishing fifth in 10.03 secs. Meanwhile, Kate O'Connor admits she is struggling to adjust to her new status as the one to beat.
