World.title: Iraqi leaders condemn attacks on Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Prominent Iraqi figures, notably Shiite cleric Muqtada al-Sadr, have openly criticized Iran-backed militias for seeking to pull Iraq into a larger regional conflict by launching unlawful drone attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia.

In a statement on X, al-Sadr strongly criticized the militias for their dangerous actions, which jeopardize the security of the Iraqi people.

Al-Sadr’s remarks came after the United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes on Iran-backed groups in several Iraqi provinces on Wednesday.

Influential Iraqi political and religious figures are escalating the pressure to disarm militant groups across the country.

The US-Saudi airstrikes were an immediate response to many drone assaults carried out by militias in the past few days against US interests in the region as well as oil facilities in Saudi Arabia.

Baghdad has initiated investigations into cross-border drone assaults in an effort to strengthen national sovereignty and prevent illegitimate military actions.

Iraqi officials confirmed that the country will not be used to launch attacks against countries in the region.

World.title: US Embassy issues new security alert, urges Americans not to travel to Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The U.S. Embassy in Baghdad on Wednesday issued a security alert advising American citizens to avoid travel to Iraq, following a series of attacks that it said were carried out by Iran-aligned militias targeting locations inside Iraq and across the region.

In the alert, the embassy urged U.S. nationals currently in Iraq to remain vigilant, closely monitor local media, and follow instructions issued by Iraqi authorities.

The embassy also warned that air travel could be affected without prior notice, including possible flight delays, cancellations, or temporary airspace closures.

As a result, American citizens planning to travel were advised to check directly with their airlines before heading to airports, as flight schedules may change at any time.

The mission reiterated that Iraq remains under the U.S. State Department’s Level 4: Do Not Travel advisory, citing terrorism, kidnapping, armed conflict, civil unrest, and the U.S. government’s limited ability to provide emergency services to its citizens in the country.

In addition to avoiding unnecessary travel, the embassy encouraged U.S. citizens already in Iraq to maintain communication with family members, ensure travel documents remain valid, and keep mobile phones fully charged.

The advisory also urged Americans to avoid protests and demonstrations, maintain a low profile, stay aware of their surroundings, and enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security updates.

Furthermore, the embassy advised citizens to follow official U.S. State Department security alerts and remain prepared for rapidly changing conditions.

The advisory comes amid heightened security tensions across Iraq and the wider region.

Earlier this week, Kurdistan Region Prime Minister Masrour Barzani said the region had recently come under drone attacks launched from the direction of Nineveh, stressing the need for an effective air defense system to protect the Kurdistan Region.

Days earlier, coalition forces intercepted eight explosive-laden drones targeting Erbil. The Kurdistan Region’s Counter-Terrorism Service said all of the drones were successfully destroyed before reaching their targets, with no casualties reported.

The U.S. Embassy continues to operate in Iraq, although the mandatory departure order for non-essential U.S. government personnel remains in effect.

World.title: Starlink officially launches satellite internet service in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Starlink officially launched its satellite internet service in Iraq on Wednesday, expanding high-speed broadband access across the country following the completion of licensing procedures with Iraq’s Communications and Media Commission (CMC).

The announcement was confirmed by CMC Chairman Balegh Abu Kalal, who declared the service officially operational.

“With God’s blessing, Starlink has officially launched in Iraq,” Abu Kalal said in a statement issued by the commission.

At the same time, Starlink updated its official service map, listing Iraq among the countries where its high-speed satellite internet service is now available.

Launch follows licensing agreement

The commercial launch comes just weeks after Iraqi authorities finalized Starlink’s operating license.

Earlier this month, Abu Kalal revealed that the licensing agreement and related security arrangements were signed inside Iraq before the government’s visit to Washington, describing the move as a step to safeguard Iraq’s digital sovereignty.

According to the CMC, the agreement requires Starlink to comply with Iraqi laws and security regulations, including cooperation with relevant authorities on licensed devices and regulatory requirements.

Government highlights security safeguards

Officials have previously said the licensing framework gives Iraqi authorities oversight of the service through agreements reached with the company and national security institutions.

The CMC also stated that Starlink agreed to comply with decisions issued by Iraq’s competent authorities, including regulations governing telecommunications services.

In addition, officials have said the agreement is intended to address the widespread use of unlicensed Starlink terminals already operating in Iraq.

Subscription prices and revenue sharing

According to previous statements by Abu Kalal, monthly subscription fees are expected to range between IQD 75,000 and IQD 150,000, depending on the service package.

The agreement also provides Iraq with a share of the company’s revenues, including an 8% direct contribution, an additional 1% universal service fee, and a 15% corporate tax applicable to telecommunications companies.

Experts see boost for digital connectivity

Technology experts have welcomed the launch, saying satellite internet could significantly improve connectivity in underserved and remote areas.

Communications infrastructure expert Redha Khudair Elias previously said Starlink plans to establish seven ground stations around Baghdad, allowing Iraqi authorities to oversee the service under the agreed regulatory framework.

Meanwhile, technology specialist Nawras Aref has urged government institutions to continue strengthening their cybersecurity capabilities to keep pace with rapidly evolving communications technologies.

Long path to market

Starlink’s entry into Iraq follows months of negotiations between Iraqi authorities and the company.

The process began under the previous government, which hosted a SpaceX delegation in December 2025 to discuss licensing for satellite internet services.

More recently, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi met Starlink executives during his visit to Washington, where Iraqi officials also signed the company’s final operating license.

The launch represents one of Iraq’s most significant telecommunications developments in recent years, with officials aiming to expand internet access while maintaining regulatory oversight of satellite-based communications.

World.title: PMF says 20 members killed, 32 injured in Joint US-Saudi airstrikes across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) on Wednesday announced that at least 20 of its members were killed and 32 others wounded in what it described as joint U.S.-Saudi airstrikes targeting its facilities across several Iraqi provinces.

In a statement, the PMF said the casualty figures remain preliminary, adding that search and damage assessment operations are still underway and the toll could rise.

According to the statement, the strikes hit official PMF headquarters in Baghdad, Wasit, Nineveh, Basra, Kirkuk, Karbala, and Diyala. The organization said the attacks also caused varying degrees of damage to military facilities, vehicles, and equipment stationed at the targeted sites.

Furthermore, the PMF described the operation as a “joint U.S.-Saudi aggression,” accusing both countries of carrying out coordinated attacks against its positions.

The PMF stressed that specialized committees continue to assess the extent of the damage and verify information from the affected locations.

As a result, it said the announced death toll of 20 members and 32 wounded represents an initial estimate that may increase as field investigations and rescue efforts continue.

The group added that comprehensive reports will be released once the assessment process is completed.

The PMF statement came hours after the U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced that American and Saudi forces had carried out coordinated airstrikes against what it described as Iran-backed militia positions across Iraq.

Saudi Arabia later confirmed its participation in the operation, saying the strikes targeted groups linked to recent drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities while emphasizing that the Kingdom does not seek further escalation.

Iraqi authorities have yet to issue a comprehensive official assessment of the reported casualties or the full impact of the strikes.

World.title: Iraqi PM cancels trip to Saudi Arabia amid security escalation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi canceled on Wednesday his trip to Saudi Arabia, which was scheduled for Thursday.

The step took place after major regional security escalations earlier in the day. The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated airstrikes targeting Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) sites in several Iraqi provinces.

The airstrikes come in response to repeated drone assaults on Saudi Arabia’s eastern oil facilities over the past few days.

Riyadh said earlier that the drone attacks were launched by Iran-backed militias inside Iraq.

An Iraqi government source told Shafaq News that all preparations for al-Zaidi’s visit to Saudi Arabia had been suspended due to the fast-paced security developments.

According to reports, al-Zaidi was scheduled to discuss the deadline set by the government on September 30 to disarm unauthorized armed organizations.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) was expected to publicly support Iraq’s efforts to impose governmental control on weaponry.

Al-Zaidi wanted to personally reassure Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that Iraqi land will not be used to attack neighboring countries.

Before the trip was canceled, al-Zaidi directed Iraq’s security services to launch an official investigation into the drone claims. However, the US-Saudi strikes prompted the suspension of diplomatic discussions.

World.title: US-Saudi strikes in Iraq kill 20 Iran-backed fighters
World.content:
Baghdad — US-Saudi strikes on Iraq on Wednesday killed at least 20 members of a former paramilitary alliance that includes pro-Iran groups, the alliance said.

The Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), an alliance of former paramilitary groups and factions now integrated into the Iraqi armed forces, said at least 20 fighters “were martyred and another 32 wounded according to a preliminary toll” following the US-Saudi strikes on its bases in seven provinces.

World.title: Search for survivors after powerful Japan quake kills 13
World.content:
Kumamoto – Rescuers battled through the tangled wreckage of a Japanese shopping mall Wednesday searching for any trapped survivors after a big earthquake killed at least 13 people.

A massive explosion ripped through the mall around 50 minutes after the 7.1-magnitude tremor on Tuesday in the southwestern Kumamoto region, where in 2016 twin quakes killed nearly 300 people.

The tremor on the island of Kyushu caused widespread damage, flattening homes, triggering fires and leaving left tens of thousands of residents without power and water.

Akio Yoshida, the president of mall operator Aeon, said three people died at the facility in the town of Kashima, with one more fatality feared and three others missing.

“The cause is still being investigated, but it’s likely that gas caused it,” fellow Aeon executive Keiji Ohno told a news conference where he and others bowed in apology.

Five people were also confirmed killed and four others were unaccounted for at the Nippon Paper Industries factory in Yatsushiro city, where part of a red-and-white smokestack collapsed, a government official told AFP.

“Extensive damage has been confirmed, including casualties, collapsed buildings, fires and damage to roads,” Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said in Tokyo as she announced 13 fatalities, describing a “race against time” to help those affected.

Government spokesman Minoru Kihara said that as of early Wednesday more than 9,000 people had sought refuge in 506 shelters in three regions of Kyushu island.

Around 130 police, 450 firefighters and 170 military personnel were involved in the rescue operation at the Aeon Mall Kumamoto, he said.

Some stunned locals said the quake was the biggest they had felt in their lifetimes, measuring at the top of Japan’s seven-level shindo scale of shakiness.

“It was the strongest quake I ever experienced,” Kanzo Matsumoto, 73, the operator of a luxury onsen hot spring inn in Yatsushiro, told AFP.

“I’m not sure if (the region) will be able to recover from the damage.”

– ‘Then an explosion’ –

Tokito Kitagawa, 21, pulled over at a convenience store when the quake struck as he was travelling in Kumamoto on his motorcycle.

“There was a sudden big noise,” Kitagawa told AFP. “I couldn’t stay standing. I had to crouch down. Then all the cup noodles fell all over me on the floor.”

One user on X who said that they worked inside the mall recounted the moments after the quake hit.

The user with the handle Palan said staff had guided customers outside and then some employees went back to get their belongings.

“Since there didn’t seem to be any smoke inside the premises from what we could see, we felt reassured,” they said. “Then an explosion occurred.”

Footage from inside the mall showed rescue workers in orange overalls and white helmets picking their way through a mass of twisted steel, dangling cables and chunks of ceiling.

Initial reports had said that as many as 20 to 30 people were trapped inside.

Some 31,200 households and facilities still had no power on Wednesday morning, while 84,000 homes were suffering water disruptions, officials said.

TV footage showed people queueing for petrol and drinking water.

– Trains suspended –

The powerful tremor, which struck at 4:27 pm (0727 GMT) on Tuesday, knocked over a cargo train, flattened a traditional “torii” gateway and cracked roads, making many impassable.

High-speed shinkansen trains mostly remained suspended on Wednesday.

Footage also showed parts of a wall at the centuries-old Kumamoto Castle collapsing.

The US Geological Survey measured the quake at 6.8, lower than Japan’s reading of 7.1.

Japan is one of the world’s most seismically active countries, sitting on top of four major tectonic plates along the western edge of the Pacific “Ring of Fire”.

Kumamoto was hit by two devastating earthquakes in 2016, which killed 273 people and injured more than 2,800.

The archipelago, home to around 125 million people, typically experiences hundreds of jolts every year and accounts for about 18 percent of the world’s earthquakes.

The vast majority are mild, although the damage they cause varies according to their location and the depth below the Earth’s surface at which they strike.

Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive 9.0-magnitude undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.

World.title: Iraq seeks to raise trade exchange with Turkey to $30 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Trade Minister Mustafa al-Ani confirmed on Tuesday that the government plans to increase trade exchange with Turkey to $30 billion.

Al-Ani’s remarks followed his meeting with Turkish Trade Minister Omer Bolat in the Turkish capital, Ankara, on the sidelines of Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s official visit to Turkey, according to a statement cited by the state-run news agency (INA).

During the meeting, the two sides confirmed their commitment to strengthening Iraq-Turkey trade and economic relations, broadening the scope of cooperation, and boosting joint investments to transform the two countries’ strategic partnership into tangible economic results serving their common interests.

The meeting focused on strategies to increase bilateral commerce to $30 billion, initiatives to support the Development Road project, and approaches to enhance transportation and customs cooperation.

The two sides also discussed the ongoing preparations for the third meeting of the Iraqi-Turkish Joint Economic and Trade Committee (JETCO III) in the fourth quarter of this year, which will strengthen the economic partnership and open up new avenues for trade and investment cooperation.

Bolat said earlier that Turkish exports to Iraq hit $8.7 billion in the first nine months of 2025, while trade between the two countries was almost $12 billion.

Turkish enterprises have undertaken 1,145 projects in Iraq, totaling $36.6 billion. This amount represents approximately 6.7 percent of their entire global project portfolio, positioning Iraq as the third-largest market for Turkish contractors worldwide.

World.title: 'Students are not terrorists, they are the future': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke asks govt to stop targeting protesters
World.content:
CJP protest in New Delhi (PTI image)

'Students won the agitation'

'If government doesn't fall in line, we'll change it'

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday urged the government to stop targeting students who participated in the nationwide protests over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying they were "not terrorists" but "the future of the country. "Speaking to reporters at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar airport after returning from Delhi, Dipke claimed that students in several states were being harassed by police even after the protests concluded."The government should behave well now. The blood of students was spilled on the streets on July 20 during the March to Parliament. Wasn't that enough? Even now, students are being troubled. In many states, police are visiting the houses of students and threatening them with arrests," he alleged, PTI cited.Dipke returned to Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar after spending nearly 36 days at Jantar Mantar, where the CJP led protests over the alleged NEET paper leak. He claimed the agitation eventually grew into a nationwide movement and resulted in the resignation of Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan."I am coming home after almost 40 days. Since I came to India, the agitations were on. Then I was at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for almost 36 days.The agitation turned out to be successful and the country's students won. I am happy that I will now meet my parents," he said.Warning the government against taking student protests lightly, Dipke said the resignation of a Union minister should not be seen as the end of the movement."These students are not terrorists. They are the future of our country. If the future of the country is treated like this, then just as Dharmendra Pradhan had to step down, tomorrow we will go and change the government if it doesn't fall in line," he said.He added that the government should not assume students' anger had subsided following the minister's resignation."If needed, we will launch a fresh agitation on a much bigger scale," Dipke said.Responding to a question, Dipke also took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, saying he should resign and become "an influencer," claiming it was "something he is very good at."

World.title: 'No abnormality found in AI Dreamliner fuel control switch locking mechanism': Govt
World.content:
The switches â which control fuel supply to engines â have been under scrutiny following AI 171 which crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad last June.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found âno abnormalityâ with the same, govt told Parliament Wednesday. The regulator had ordered this repeat examination following the crew operating an AI Dreamliner (VT-ANX) from London to Bengaluru this Feb had observed an issue with the switch after landing safely and had reported the same.These switches â which control fuel supply to engines â have been under scrutiny following AI 171 which crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad last June as its engines had run out of fuel. While why that happened is still being probed, the locking system of fuel control switches has been probed multiple times since then to ensure safety on other Dreamliners operating around the world and are still being looked at by Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) which is probing AI 171 crash. The Dreamliner is the most widely used mid-range wide body aircraft globally.âDGCA, as part of continued airworthiness, directed original equipment manufacturer (OEM) level testing of fuel control switch locking mechanism in Seattle.Detailed examination of fuel control switch including structural integrity of fuel control switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed,â Union minister of state for aviation Murlidhar Mohol said in a parliamentary reply Wednesday.However, the minister added that âfurther inspection of complete thrust control module at OEM facility is underwayâ. This module translates pilot inputs or autothrottle commands into precise electronic signals to control engine power.On Feb 2, 2026, the AI Dreamliner on which the crew had reported an issue with the fuel control switch after landing in Bengaluru had been grounded for checks. At that time AI had said in a statement: âWe are aware that one of our pilots has reported a possible defect on the fuel control switch of a Boeing 787-8 aircraft. After receiving this initial information, we have grounded the said aircraft and are involving the original equipment manufacturer (OEM) to get the pilotâs concerns checked on a priority basis. The matter has been communicated to the aviation regulator, DGCA. Air India had checked the fuel control switches on all Boeing 787 aircraft in its fleet after a directive from the DGCA, and had found no issues.âThe AI 171 crash preliminary investigation report of the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau had said: âIn the cockpit voice recording, one of the pilots is heard asking the other why did he cutoff (the fuel control switch).The other pilot responded that he did not do so,â says.Meanwhile, on Wednesday about the AI 171 crash probe Mohol said: âThere is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process involving multiple variables. The investigation is under progress. All probable causes and contributing factors leading to the accident are being investigated. The final investigation report (including all the findings) will be made public and published on. AAIB website after completion of the investigation.â

World.title: Half of country’s chief ministers face criminal cases: ADR-NEW Report
World.content:
CHENNAI: A report released by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and the National Election Watch (NEW) has revealed that nearly half of the country's chief ministers face criminal cases.

According to the findings, 14 (45%) of the 31 chief ministers, nearly half of them, have declared criminal cases against themselves.

More concerning is that 11 chief ministers (35%), one-third of them, face serious criminal charges, including offences carrying maximum punishments of five years or more, non-bailable cognizable offences, assault, murder, kidnapping, crimes against women, and violations under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Notably, two chief ministers have declared cases related to 'attempt to murder'.

The average assets per chief minister stand at a staggering Rs 118.07 crore. Out of the 31 chief ministers analysed, four (13%) are billionaires with declared assets crossing Rs 100 crore.

Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar tops the list as the wealthiest, with total assets exceeding Rs 1,413 crore, followed by Andhra Pradesh chief minister Chandrababu Naidu (Rs 931 crores+), Tamil Nadu's C

(Rs 648 crores+), and Arunachal Pradesh's Pema Khandu (Rs 332 crores+).





The average assets per chief minister stand at a staggering Rs 118.07 crore. Out of the 31 chief ministers analysed, four (13%) are billionaires with declared assets crossing Rs 100 crore. At the other end of the spectrum, Jammu and Kashmir's Omar Abdullah declared the lowest assets at Rs 55.24 lakhs, followed by West Bengal's Suvendu Adhikari (Rs 85.87 lakh) and Rajasthan's Bhajan Lal Sharma (Rs 1.46 crore). Out of the 31 chief ministers evaluated, Rekha Gupta (Delhi) is the sole woman chief minister.

Majority of chief ministers are well-educated. Postgraduates form the largest segment at 29% (nine), followed by graduates at 23% (seven), graduate professionals at 19% (six), doctorates at 10% (three), and Class 10 or 12 pass accounting for the remainder.

The analysis based on self-sworn affidavits filed by all 31 incumbent chief ministers before contesting their respective last elections has brought to light striking details regarding their criminal backgrounds, financial status and education across India's 28 states and 3 Union territories. World.title: Rahul Gandhi's remarks on student protests trigger Parliament showdown: What happened next
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Amid repeated disruptions, sloganeering and adjournments, the Lok Sabha on Wednesday passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to impose stricter punishment for paper leaks and examination-related offences.

The debate, which resumed after days of deadlock, quickly turned into a political showdown after leader of opposition

attacked the government over the police action during the July 20 student protests, drawing sharp rebuttals from the treasury benches.

Here are the top developments:

Rahul

targets Amit Shah, RSS

Participating in the debate on the Bill, Rahul Gandhi took a direct swipe at Union home minister Amit Shah, claiming his absence from the House reflected "fear".

"I am very happy today to see that the so-called home minister of this country does not have the courage to come and sit here... Why is the home minister not here today? The home minister is not here today because he is scared," Rahul said.

"The home minister authorised the shooting on our students. He put pellets into the blood of our students. He ordered the students of India to be shot," he alleged.

Launching another attack on the government, Rahul said India's education system was "terrible" and "cruel" and accused the Centre of privatising education.





"Our education system is terrible, it's cruel... Everything is being privatised... It is an extortion system, it is a brutal, terrible system," he said.

Alleging that the RSS is controlling the education ministry, Rahul said, "The soul of the system has been captured by the RSS. The resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan is superficial because Dharmendra Pradhan never ran the education ministry. The organisation that runs the education ministry is called the RSS.

The man who runs it is an OSD sitting in the minister's office," Rahul said.

He further claimed students were not being allowed to pursue their passions or question the system and were instead being forced to accept "the nonsensical history that the RSS fantasises about."

Remarks spark uproar, partially expunged

Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju objected to Rahul Gandhi's remarks and demanded an apology.

"On what basis have you said this? This is highly objectionable.

You should apologise," Rijiju said.

Speaker

immediately intervened, reminding Rahul that the discussion was not on the home minister.

"We are not discussing the Home Minister today," Birla said, asking the Congress leader to provide evidence to substantiate his allegations.

Parts of Rahul Gandhi's speech were later expunged from the House records.

The Lok Sabha was also adjourned twice amid uproar over his remarks.

Government hits back

Union commerce minister

accused Rahul Gandhi of making "baseless" and "false" allegations over the alleged police action on students.

"It was nothing but a bundle of lies. He should not be allowed to get away with this. Rahul Gandhi should apologise. This is a serious misuse of the House," Goyal told reporters in the Parliament complex.

"There was no firing at all. How can Rahul Gandhi make such false allegations? He should apologise in the House and apologise to the country," he said.

Calling Rahul "frustrated", Goyal claimed students had "rejected" the Congress leader.

"There is no cure for some people. The Leader of the Opposition made such baseless and false statements on the floor of the House. There was no firing, yet such baseless allegations were made inside Parliament. I strongly condemn it," he added.

Jitendra Singh criticises Rahul

Replying to the debate, Union Minister Jitendra Singh accused Rahul Gandhi of politicising the issue instead of participating in a constructive discussion.

"This legislation has been brought with great sensitivity and reflects the commitment of Prime Minister

Narendra Modi

towards ensuring fairness in public examinations. Instead of participating in a constructive discussion or offering suggestions, the Opposition is trying to politicise the issue," Singh said.

He also criticised Rahul's conduct in Parliament.

"I am surprised by the behaviour of the leader of the opposition.

The kind of language he used in Parliament was inappropriate. Such expressions should not be used in the House," he said.

Singh further said Rahul appeared unaware of basic parliamentary procedures despite occupying the post of Leader of Opposition.

"The office of the leader of the opposition carries great respect. It is surprising that he does not seem to know the basic norms of Parliament," he said.

Referring to Rahul's allegation against Amit Shah, Singh said no minister could order police action.

"When Rahul Gandhi claims that Amit Shah ordered action against students, he has failed to provide any evidence. For basic information, no minister can issue such orders. Such decisions are taken by a magistrate, District Magistrate (DM), or Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). This is basic administrative knowledge, and it appears he lacks even this understanding," Singh said.

Bill passed with tougher penalties

The Lok Sabha later passed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 after Jitendra Singh's reply.

The Bill proposes to increase the punishment for those using unfair means in public examinations to a minimum of five years' imprisonment, extendable up to ten years, compared to the existing provision of three to five years.

It also seeks to raise the maximum fine for offenders from Rs 10 lakh to Rs 50 lakh.

For service providers found involved in examination-related offences, the maximum fine has been proposed to be increased from the existing level to Rs 5 crore, while the debarment period from conducting public examinations will be doubled from four years to eight years.

For organised examination-related crimes, the Amendment Bill proposes imprisonment of not less than seven years, extendable up to ten years, along with a maximum fine of Rs 10 crore, up from the existing Rs 1 crore.

The Bill also empowers the Centre to constitute a Special Task Force to investigate paper leaks and other examination-related offences.

In addition, it proposes a new Section 12A mandating completion of investigations within two months, day-to-day trials in designated Special Fast Track Courts to be completed within three months of filing the charge sheet, and the appointment of Special Public Prosecutors for every such court.

Rahul addresses media

After the day's proceedings, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of denying him an opportunity to speak in the Lok Sabha because he held Union home minister Amit Shah responsible for the alleged police brutality during the July 20 CJP march.

Addressing a press conference, Rahul claimed he was assured he would be allowed to resume his speech if he apologised, but said he refused, declaring that he would "never ever apologise to the BJP, RSS, or any other person associated with them."

"As you saw today, the leader of the opposition was not allowed to speak in the Lok Sabha. Multiple times, I asked the Speaker to bring order to the House so that I could speak. Multiple times, Rajnath Singh ji and others were allowed to speak, but I was not allowed to speak. The excuse was that I said something about Mr. Amit Shah. I said that Mr. Amit Shah was responsible for the brutality that was carried out," Rahul said.

During the press conference, Rahul called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack Amit Shah over the alleged crackdown on student protesters and demanded an independent probe into the incident, which is being monitored by the Supreme Court.

He also claimed the Congress had gathered evidence showing that police used electric batons, pellet guns and lathis fitted with nails to disperse students.

"They were shot with pellet guns. One boy who was shot with a pellet gun is most likely to lose his eye and may not be able to see. I have seen the AIIMS medical certificate, which shows that he was shot with pellet guns. Shock batons were used, not just normal lathis, lathis with nails.

Where did the police get this idea from?" Rahul said.

"Now there are two possibilities. Either Amit Shah gave the order to shoot people with pellet guns, beat people with lathis with nails, and use electric batons, or he did not know it was happening. If he did not know, he is incompetent. If he ordered it, he is culpable. In either case, he has to go. And every single child who has been beaten must know this," he added.

BJP hits back

Reacting to Rahul's remarks, BJP MP Sambit Patra defended the objections raised by treasury bench members during the Congress leader's speech in the Lok Sabha.

"Rahul Gandhi alleged that Kiren Rijiju and Rajnath Singh interrupted him, while he himself was not given an opportunity to speak. First of all, the two or three objections raised by Kiren Rijiju were entirely justified. Those objections were regarding the use of the unparliamentary word 'idiot', which, under the rules of Parliament, cannot be used on the floor of the House. As the Parliamentary Affairs Minister, it was his responsibility to seek clarification on that.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Kiren Rijiju's demeanour, body language, and choice of words reflected decency, humility, and composure. He was not angry. In a calm manner, he said, 'We want to hear you. Please do not use the word "idiot", because the House functions according to parliamentary rules.' Defence minister Rajnath Singh made only one appeal. He said, 'Rahul ji, please speak,' and appealed to the members of the treasury benches to listen to Rahul Gandhi carefully.

What greater example of democratic tradition could there be than that?" Patra said.

Small triggers, large fuses:

BENGALURU: In May 2026, the Chief Justice of India made an offhand, dismissive remark about unemployed young Indians being like cockroaches. Ten weeks later, a Union minister had resigned, tens of thousands of protesters had marched on Parliament, and a satirical party named after the insult was the biggest story in the country â not necessarily in that order!Nobody involved in that first remark could have predicted where it would end up. That gap, between how small these things start and how large they end up, is the story of Indian student politics itself.It is, in fact, the pattern that connects nearly every major student agitation since independence, laid out in the timeline alongside this piece. A hostel mess-fee hike in Ahmedabad brought down a state govt. A poetry reading on a university lawn became a national argument about sedition.A single self-immolation outside a Delhi college reshaped a decade of caste politics. Indian students, again and again, have turned small, local sparks into fires. Not because the sparks themselves were extraordinary, but because they landed on reservoirs of frustration, economic distress, discrimination, corruption, a sense of being unheard, that were already primed to catch. Few groups in Indian public life have intervened so often, so unpredictably, or with such little warning.India has one of the youngest populations in the world, and its colleges concentrate huge numbers of young people in one place, with time and energy that older, more encumbered protesters often canât spare â but it isnât that students have less at stake.Itâs that whatâs at stake for them is the future itself: the job market theyâre about to enter, the country theyâre about to inherit, the fairness of the exam or the quota or the citizenship rule that will decide their next decade.Campuses also come with built-in organising infrastructure: hostels, unions, canteens, and, increasingly, group chats that can turn a local grievance into a national one within hours. Students also carry a kind of moral capital unlike any other in Indian public culture: the idea, inherited from the independence movement itself, that young people protesting is a sign of a healthy conscience rather than a threat to order.But structure alone doesn't explain the pattern. India has produced at least 13 agitations substantial enough to, in different ways, influence Indian politics since 1947 â from the 1959 Bengal food riots to the Cockroach Movement. Look closely at five of them across seven decades, and a consistent anatomy emerges: the way these movements start, escalate, provoke the state, and either win, lose, or curdle into something else.In Dec 1973, students at an Ahmedabad engineering college struck over a 20% hike in hostel mess fees. Layered onto soaring food prices and corruption allegations against the stateâs chief minister, the strike metastasised within weeks into the Navnirman Andolan. Curfews were imposed in 44 towns; the army was deployed.Facing sustained pressure, chief minister Chimanbhai Patel resigned in Feb 1974, and when the assembly wouldnât dissolve on its own, veteran leader Morarji Desaiâs hunger strike and continued student pressure forced fresh elections anyway. It remains the only instance in independent Indiaâs history of sustained public agitation toppling an elected govt outright â and as per multiple accounts, it directly inspired Jayaprakash Narayanâs (JP) much larger Bihar Movement weeks later, which fed into the political climate that produced both the 1975 Emergency and Congressâ historic 1977 defeat.After electoral rolls turned up apparent non-citizens, the All Assam Studentsâ Union launched a movement demanding detection and deportation of illegal immigrants. What followed is among the longest continuous student-led agitations in Indian history: blockades, election boycotts, and periods of horrific ethnic violence, including the 1983 Nellie massacre, in a movement whose overall toll has been estimated above 850 deaths.It ended with the 1985 Assam Accord, which set a cutoff date for citizenship claims and promised cultural safeguards still only partially delivered today. AASU leaders converted the movement into a political party, the Asom Gana Parishad, and won the state election that followed.When the govt moved to implement the Mandal Commissionâs 27% OBC quota in central jobs, upper-caste students across northern India erupted in protest. On Sept 19, 1990, 19-year-old Delhi University student Rajeev Goswami set himself on fire outside his college; he survived with severe burns but never fully recovered. His act triggered a wave of copycat self-immolation attempts nationwide. The quota was implemented anyway, and VP Singhâs govt fell within months for reasons beyond Mandal alone â proof that a movement can dominate the national imagination for years without reversing the policy that provoked it.Student-led sit-ins against the Citizenship Amendment Act spread from Jamia Millia Islamia to campuses nationwide, but the defining moment came on the night of Dec 15, 2019, when Delhi Police entered Jamiaâs campus, including its library, and used batons and tear gas on students inside. That single raid, captured on phone cameras, played an important role in nationalising the anti-CAA movement than months of organizing had. The law remained on the statute books and was later notified, even though the protests fundamentally reshaped the national debate.A dismissive remark about unemployed youth being like âcockroachesâ was turned into satire by a strategist who founded the Cockroach Janata Party â a parody of the ruling partyâs name, with an AI-generated mascot. Fuelled by anger over leaked entrance exams and graduate unemployment near 40%, it grew from an online joke to hundreds of thousands of members within weeks. On July 20, 2026, roughly 20,000 protesters tried to march on Parliament; police used tear gas and batons, injuring nearly 180 people.Rather than back down, the movement camped at Jantar Mantar and spread to a dozen cities. On July 25, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned â the core demand met in about ten weeks, a fraction of the time earlier movements took to win anything at all.The five above are the clearest cases, but the other eight matter just as much.s â there had already been other student protests in places like Travancore and Hyderabad â when a famine-level food crisis and police firing on a mass rally pulled students into the streets alongside workers and peasants â establishing, for the first time, that this kind of politics was legitimate in the new republic.Student-led protests against the imposition of Hindi as the sole official language ultimately led the govt to guarantee English would continue indefinitely, and permanently reshaped Tamil Naduâs politics around the DMK., saw students mobilise around regional neglect and job inequities decades before the state itself was created in 2014 â a reminder that some of these movements take generations to pay off, if they ever do., is where JPâs âTotal Revolutionâ turned a student agitation against corruption and unemployment into a national coalition; when Indira Gandhi responded by declaring the Emergency in 1975, students â opposition parties, socialists, RSS cadres, trade unions also operated from underground â were among groups that kept organised dissent alive underground until elections finally returned in 1977., saw medical and engineering students protest the extension of OBC quotas to central higher-education institutions. The courts upheld most provisions of the policy in 2008, making this the direct sequel to 1990âs argument, fought with less violence but the same underlying tension., wasnât organised by any student union â it was a largely leaderless, student-heavy public eruption after the gangrape and murder of a young physiotherapy student (Nirbhaya case), and one of the rare cases here that produced fast legislative change: the 2013 criminal law reforms toughening rape sentencing., was smaller in scale but longer in duration: FTII students struck for 139 days over the appointment of a chairman they saw as a political pick, keeping alive the broader argument about political interference in public institutions even though the appointment itself stood., delivered two separate shocks in one year: Dalit scholar Rohith Vemulaâs suicide, after his suspension amid political pressure, reopened a national reckoning over caste discrimination on campus. Weeks later, the arrest of JNU Studentsâ Union president Kanhaiya Kumar on sedition charges, after a campus event, turned âanti-nationalâ speech into one of the decadeâs defining and most polarising arguments.Four patterns recur across all thirteen movements above, not just the five examined in depth.As the opening of this piece argued, the size of the spark has never predicted the size of the fire. What decides that is how much pre-existing frustration was already sitting there, waiting for something to ignite it.In case after case, the decisive escalation wasnât the original grievance but the visible use of force against students: police firing in Calcutta in 1959 and Madurai in 1965, the Jamia library raid in 2019, the tear-gassing at Jantar Mantar in 2026. Violence against students, especially once captured on camera, has repeatedly turned local protests into national ones and made the state's own response the story.Self-immolation recurs across this history, most starkly in 1990, as a form of protest with few real parallels in other democraciesâ student movements â a sign both of the intensity of feeling involved and of a media culture in which one person's extreme act can shift public opinion faster than a rally of thousands.Of the 13 movements above, only Navnirman clearly toppled a govt outright. A handful won specific, bounded concessions â the 1965 language guarantee, the 2013 rape-law reforms, Pradhan's 2026 resignation. Several others, including Mandal, the JNU sedition case, and Anti-CAA, ended without the underlying policy being reversed at all, even as they reshaped public debate for years.The honest lesson of seventy years of student politics is that these movements are far better at forcing a national conversation, or costing one official their job, than at reversing a government's core commitments. What has changed is speed, not shape. In 1974 and 1990, it took months or years for a local grievance to become a national reckoning, carried by hostel meetings and cyclostyled pamphlets.In 2026, it took ten weeks, carried by a meme and a mascot. The grammar is identical either way: a grievance, a trigger, a confrontation with the state, and an outcome judged by whether it produced a resignation, a repealed law, or just a memory.

World.title: Rahul Gandhi's 'advice' to PM Modi, and 3 guarantees to students over police action on protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday accused the Centre of denying him an opportunity to speak in the Lok Sabha because he held Union home minister Amit Shah responsible for the alleged police brutality during the July 20 CJP march.

Addressing a press conference after the proceedings, Rahul claimed he was assured he would be allowed to resume his speech if he apologised, but said he refused, declaring that he would "never ever apologise to the BJP, RSS, or any other person associated with them."

"As you saw today, the leader of the opposition was not allowed to speak in the Lok Sabha. Multiple times, I asked the Speaker to bring order to the House so that I could speak.

Multiple times, Rajnath Singh ji and others were allowed to speak, but I was not allowed to speak. The excuse was that I said something about Mr. Amit Shah. I said that Mr. Amit Shah was responsible for the brutality that was carried out," Rahul said.

"I was also given an assurance that if I apologise, I will be allowed to continue speaking. The first thing is, I will never ever apologise to the BJP, RSS, or any other person associated with them.





The second thing is, it is my right as the Leader of the Opposition to raise issues that are important for this country. To me, the most important issue today is that our students, people who are open-minded and ask questions, were brutalised on the streets of Delhi," he added.

'Sack Shah, order probe'

During the conference, Rahul called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi to sack Amit Shah over the alleged crackdown on student protesters and demanded an independent probe into the incident, which is being monitored by the Supreme Court.

He also claimed the Congress had gathered evidence showing that police used electric batons, pellet guns and lathis fitted with nails to disperse students.

"They were shot with pellet guns. One boy who was shot with a pellet gun is most likely to lose his eye and may not be able to see. I have seen the AIIMS medical certificate, which shows that he was shot with pellet guns. Shock batons were used, not just normal lathis, lathis with nails.

Where did the police get this idea from?" Rahul said.

"Now there are two possibilities. Either Amit Shah gave the order to shoot people with pellet guns, beat people with lathis with nails, and use electric batons, or he did not know it was happening. If he did not know, he is incompetent. If he ordered it, he is culpable. In either case, he has to go. And every single child who has been beaten must know this," he added.

"We are not asking for anything that is out of the ordinary. At least have the decency to take responsibility for what you have done," he further said.

3 promises to students

During the press conference, Rahul Gandhi also made three promises to students affected by the alleged police action. He said the he would ensure justice for the injured students, punish those responsible for the alleged use of pellet guns, and hold those involved accountable.

"We will ensure that the students who were beaten, maybe not today, maybe sometime from now, but we will ensure that every single one of those students who was beaten gets justice," he said.

"We will ensure that the people who shot our students with pellet guns will be punished. It's very simple for us to do. We have the photographs. We've collected all the videos and all the photographs. We know the police officers who have done it," Rahul said.

"So, you might think you're very smart, but accountability is going to come. This is our guarantee. This is our guarantee to the students," he said.

World.title: SC grants bail to two alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives after 12 years
World.content:
Supreme Court grants bail to two accused of operating under Indian Mujahideen (ANI image)

Court notes overlapping FIRs

Bail subject to conditions

Background of the case

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has granted bail to two alleged Indian Mujahideen operatives who have been in custody since 2014, holding that their prolonged incarceration without the trial nearing completion was a violation of their fundamental right to liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta granted relief to Mohd Saquib Ansari and Waqar Azhar, who had challenged an April order of the Delhi high court rejecting their bail pleas in a terror case registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell in November 2011.In its July 27 order, the apex court observed that the two accused had spent nearly 12 years in custody with little progress in the trial."...we feel that the continued incarceration of the petitioners in this case is grossly violative of the right to liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution of India," the Bench said.The court also noted that the trial had progressed at an extremely slow pace and there was no immediate prospect of its conclusion. It further pointed out that one of the co-accused had already been granted bail.The Bench observed that the petitioners had been arrested in connection with three FIRs, including two registered in Rajasthan, and had remained in custody since 2014.It said the allegations in the three cases substantially overlapped."Having appreciated the submissions advanced at bar and upon going through the record, we find that the petitioners have, more or less, been implicated in three separate FIRs for overlapping allegations," the court said.The court directed that Ansari and Azhar be released on bail in connection with the Delhi case on terms and conditions to be decided by the trial court, provided they are not required in any other case.The Bench directed the accused to continue cooperating with the trial and said the prosecution would be free to approach the Supreme Court if they attempted to delay proceedings, failed to cooperate or misused the liberty granted to them.The court also clarified that its observations were limited to deciding the bail applications and should not be treated as comments on the merits of the case.Ansari and Azhar had challenged the Delhi high court's April 24 order rejecting their bail pleas after the trial court had also denied them relief.While refusing bail, the high court observed that the two were active members of the banned terrorist organisation Indian Mujahideen and key operatives of its Rajasthan module. It also noted that they allegedly had links with the outfit's leadership in both India and Pakistan.The duo was arrested by the Delhi Police Special Cell in March 2014 and booked under provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

World.title: Holiday for educational institutions in Kerala’s Wayanad
World.content: Educational institutions in Wayanad will get a holiday on Thursday (July 30, 2026) in view of the India Meteorological department declaring an orange alert forecasting heavy to very heavy rainfall in the district on the day. They include anganwadis, tuition centres, professional colleges, and religious classes. However, it is not applicable to residential schools and colleges.

World.title: Cockroach Janta Party seeks 15% education budget, faster fee reimbursements in Telangana
World.content:
Buoyed by what it described as a victory in its 36-day protest in New Delhi that ended with the resignation of former Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) Telangana unit on Wednesday said it would now shift its focus to educational reforms in the State. Its demands include increasing education spending, expediting fee reimbursement, fast-tracking investigations into paper leak cases and implementing the recommendations of former Telangana Education Commission chairman Akunuri Murali.

Addressing a gathering at People’s Plaza in Hyderabad, CJP Telangana representative Vijay Mallangi said the movement would continue beyond the developments in Delhi. “Our agenda now is to fight for educational reforms in Telangana. We want a minimum of 15% of the State budget to be allocated to education, fee reimbursement to be released at the earliest and all paper leak cases in Telangana to be thoroughly investigated. Any pending investigations should be fast-tracked. We also want the recommendations of former Telangana Education Commission chairman Akunuri Murali to be implemented this year instead of remaining confined to government files,” he said.

He added that the party would engage with student organisations across the State to prepare a student charter highlighting key concerns before taking it up with the CJP leadership.

The party had organised the gathering to celebrate what it described as the success of its nationwide agitation over alleged irregularities in National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test and the subsequent resignation of Mr.Pradhan.

CJP members had also planned to march from People’s Plaza to the Ambedkar statue to pay tribute to students who allegedly died by suicide over examination-related issues. However, the march could not be held after the organisers said they were denied permission by the police.

According to Mr. Mallangi, the organisers had applied for permission on Tuesday, informing the authorities that around 300 people would participate in a peaceful gathering with a sound system. He alleged that shortly before the event began, they were informed permission had not been granted and that they would not be allowed to proceed with the march or use the sound system.

Speaking at the event, Sreeja of the Disha Students Organisation questioned the selective action taken over social media posts. She asked why action was initiated only against citizens critical of the government while posts targeting people based on religion, caste or containing derogatory remarks against political leaders often went unaddressed.

The gathering also featured slogans in support of Telangana and the nation, including ‘Jai Telangana’ and ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’. Protesters displayed placards on various issues, including one reading, ‘I take both my fuel and Coke sugar free’, drawing attention to concerns over ethanol blending in fuel. The programme concluded with participants singing and dancing to Gaddar’s iconic song Podusthunna Poddumeeda while raising slogans.

World.title: GRP, RPF seize 16.92 kg marijuana at Hyderabad railway station, one held
World.content:
HYDERABAD

The Government Railway Police (GRP), Hyderabad, and the Railway Protection Force (RPF) arrested a 20-year-old inter-State drug courier and seized 16.92 kg of marijuana worth an estimated ₹8.46 lakh at Hyderabad railway station on Tuesday.

The accused, identified as Akash Singh, a native of Jaunpur district in Uttar Pradesh, was apprehended during a joint checking drive near the entrance to platform no. 4. Another suspect accompanying him managed to escape.

During interrogation, Akash allegedly told the police that he had agreed to transport marijuana from Visakhapatnam to New Delhi for ₹15,000 per trip at the behest of a man identified as Jafar. He allegedly travelled to Visakhapatnam, where two bags containing the contraband were handed over to him before he boarded the Godavari Express for New Delhi.

Police said Akash and another accused, identified as Manish, arrived at Hyderabad railway station on Tuesday morning, where they came under suspicion during the checking drive. While Manish escaped, Akash was apprehended with two bags containing 16.92 kg of marijuana.

The police seized 14 packets of marijuana concealed in two bags along with a mobile phone. A case has been registered under Sections 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(B) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act.

Police identified three other accused, Jafar, Miya and Manish, as absconding. Further investigation is under way.

World.title: Indiscipline will not be tolerated, says TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Rao
World.content:
TDP State president Palla Srinivasa Raohas made it clear that every leader and activist must adhere to the rules, ideology and policies without fail, and not cause any embarrassment to the party when speaking about matters pertaining to it.

Party national president N. Chandrababu Naidu issued explicit orders that leaders should not share stage with YSR Congress Party leaders, except under certain exceptional circumstances, Mr. Srinivasa Rao said while addressing the media at the TDP central office, near Mangalagiri, on Wednesday.

Mr. Srinivasa Rao said the party would not tolerate indiscipline, and it was closely monitoring every development. The party was calling for explanations whenever required, and it was not hesitant to take disciplinary action against those crossing the line. Even if mistakes were committed unintentionally, such instances should not repeat.

He said every leader should remember that the party was above all and no one should behave in such a manner that brings disrepute to it, or members of the ruling coalition (BJP and Jana Sena Party). Each one in the party must work with achieving victory in the 2029 elections as the single-minded goal and take development and welfare schemes to the people.

Referring to MLA Bonda Umamaheswara Rao sharing the stage with a YSRCP leader (a former Minister), Mr. Srinivasa Rao said the party leadership expressed displeasure at what happened, but upon an assurance that he would hereafter strictly adhere to the rules of conduct, the matter had been closed.

World.title: Woman admits to abandoning newborn found dead in Kerala’s Nilambur
World.content:
A 28-year-old woman has admitted to abandoning her newborn after the baby’s body was found inside a waste bucket in the toilet of a private hospital at Akampadam near Nilambur, the police said.

The woman, a native of Chaliyar, is under police custody at the District Hospital, Nilambur. Medical examination confirmed that she had recently given birth. During questioning, she reportedly told the police that the baby was stillborn.

The body of the full-term baby boy was discovered on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) morning by a hospital worker while cleaning the toilet.

According to preliminary investigation, the woman arrived at the hospital around Monday (July 27, 2026) midnight with her husband and relatives, complaining of excessive bleeding.

The police said neither she nor her family disclosed that she was pregnant. As no female doctor was available, the hospital staff advised them to shift her to another hospital.

According to the police, the woman entered the toilet claiming that she wanted to change her clothes, delivered the baby there, placed the infant in a waste bucket, covered it, and left around 45 minutes later.

She was then taken to the District Hospital at Nilambur, where she reportedly did not reveal that she had given birth.

The police said the woman had not informed her family about the pregnancy. Her husband, who works in the Gulf, had returned home four days earlier. This was her third delivery.

The police registered a case of unnatural death. They said detailed statements would be recorded from the woman, her husband, and other family members. Further investigation will continue after the newborn’s post-mortem.

World.title: Kerala health university to launch four major projects on Friday
World.content:
The Kerala University of Health Sciences (KUHS) will launch four major academic and development initiatives on Friday. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan will inaugurate the projects at a function to be held on the university campus at Mulangunnathukavu.

The Minister will formally inaugurate the MSc Medical Bioinformatics programme, a pioneering initiative that is expected to strengthen interdisciplinary medical education in Kerala. The programme is being offered under the School of Translational Health Sciences, established at the university’s headquarters. It is the first on-campus academic programme of KUHS and also the first postgraduate programme in Medical Bioinformatics in Kerala.

Since its inception, KUHS has been promoting excellence in health sciences education through its affiliated institutions. The launch of an academic programme on its own campus marks a new chapter in the university’s academic journey and reflects its commitment to advancing interdisciplinary education, research and innovation in health sciences, according to a press release from KUHS.

The Minister will also dedicate to the State the medicinal plant garden established on the university campus with financial assistance from the National Medicinal Plants Board (NMPB). The garden, which will serve as a valuable resource for students, researchers and faculty members, is expected to promote biodiversity conservation, medicinal plant research and public health awareness.

Another major initiative to be launched is the University’s dedicated YouTube channel for public health awareness. The channel aims to disseminate scientifically validated health information, promote healthy lifestyles and counter misinformation related to diseases, treatments and preventive healthcare through expert talks, interviews and awareness programmes.

The Minister will also inaugurate the university’s state-of-the-art e-learning studio, which has been established to facilitate masterclasses, digital learning resources and other technology-enabled academic initiatives for students. Mohanan Kunnummal, Vice-Chancellor, will preside over the function.

World.title: Spate of violent assaults raises public safety concerns in Kochi
World.content:
A string of violent incidents involving people with criminal records reported from different parts of the city over the past few months has triggered fresh concerns over public safety. At least one such case in which people, including women, were attacked by such groups has been reported from the city almost every month since March.

Two back-to-back group assault cases, allegedly triggered by road rage, were reported from near Kakkanad in the past two weeks. While three men, two of them history-sheeters, have been arrested for allegedly brutally assaulting three youths following a dispute over road space on Sunday, four identifiable people have been booked for allegedly beating up a 52-year-old man in a similar incident on July 22.

In June, two young women were allegedly harassed and physically assaulted in Kaloor during early hours, after they objected to lewd gestures and verbal abuse near a tea shop. The police subsequently arrested multiple suspects. In May-end, a police team was injured after they allegedly came under attack from a group of youths, suspected to be in an inebriated state, near Marottichodu at Unichira. Early in May, a woman was allegedly assaulted at knifepoint near the Ernakulam Junction Railway Station, leading to two arrests. In March, a three-member gang allegedly assaulted an employee of a teashop as they were provoked by the delay in giving them cigarettes.

Sources with the city police said such incidents kept occurring despite frequent patrols. Officers said most of the recent incidents involving groups occurred following sudden provocations and often under the influence of intoxicants. “None of the recent cases were planned attacks. However, they create a sense of fear among people who have to go out at night,” conceded an officer with the city police.

The officer said repeat offenders were being tracked consistently, and strict action including invocation of the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act was being taken against them.

The Ernakulam Rural police, meanwhile, said they had been cracking down on goons and history-sheeters under Operation Steel Bird, a special drive launched in March.

District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) K.S. Sudarshan said 22 alleged habitual offenders had been arrested since March under the operation launched to prevent organised crime.

“Special teams have been constituted for intelligence gathering and tracking wanted accused. Surveillance on habitual offenders has been intensified, and preventive arrests will be made to stop crimes before they are committed. The department will also initiate steps to seek cancellation of bail granted to the arrested accused in their earlier criminal cases,” Mr. Sudarshan said.

World.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned twice as Opposition demands Amit Shah’s presence over protest crackdown
World.content:
The Rajya Sabha failed to function in the first half of Wednesday (July 29, 2026), with the House being adjourned twice as Opposition members questioned the absence of Home Minister Amit Shah.

Also read | Lok Sabha clears anti-paper leak amendment Bill amid Opposition din

They demanded a statement from him on the July 20 police action against protesters as well as on the presence of Delhi Police at the Communist Party of India (Marxist) headquarters to arrest Jawaharlal Nehru University Student Union president Aishe Ghosh on Tuesday (July 28, 2026).

The first adjournment came within 20 minutes of the House assembling for the day. The second followed shortly after noon.

‘Democracy under threat’

The day’s proceedings began with Opposition members protesting the entry of Delhi Police personnel into the CPI(M) headquarters in Delhi to arrest Ms. Ghosh in connection with a 2021 JNU protest case. Raising the issue, CPI(M) member John Brittas claimed that the arrest was prompted by Ms. Ghosh’s recent participation in the demonstration at Jantar Mantar. He said a Delhi Police team in plainclothes had entered the party office to make the arrest.

Supporting him, Leader of the Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge said democracy was under threat.

Responding to the charge, Leader of the House J.P. Nadda described the arrest as a routine law-and-order matter and said the police had acted according to procedure. He added that students involved in activism often faced such action, recalling that he himself had been picked up by the police from his classroom during the Emergency imposed by the Indira Gandhi government.

Amid the uproar, the House was adjourned till noon.

‘Where is the Home Minister?’

When the House reassembled for Question Hour, Treasury and Opposition benches again clashed after Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury drew attention to Mr. Shah’s absence.

“Where is the Home Minister? Call him here,” Ms. Chowdhury said. “You fire at students,” she added, as Opposition members raised slogans demanding that Mr. Shah come to the House.

Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan then adjourned the House till 2 p.m.

The Rajya Sabha has remained largely non-functional since the Monsoon Session began on July 20 amid continuing confrontations between the government and the Opposition.

World.title: The biggest jaundice myth most Indians still believe: ‘…is not how we treat hepatitis’
World.content:
LiverDoc, aka hepatologist Cyriac Abby Philips, took to X to bust the myth that jaundice, which is not a disease and is a symptom of a disease, can be liver-related or non-liver-related.

“Just want to pitch in here (again, sigh). This is a long-standing myth in South Asia when it comes to jaundice. Jaundice is not a disease; it’s the symptom of a disease. It can be liver-related or non-liver-related. Acute hepatitis leading to jaundice is the most common cause of jaundice in India. It’s due to food and water borne viruses. These are self-limiting. Meaning it will go away in a few days to weeks and does not require treatment. But it does require nutrition. Going on a bland diet, eating boiled food, sustaining on vegetables and avoiding oil is not how we treat jaundice or hepatitis,” he stressed in a post on X.



According to Philips, one should eat well, eat more… eat carbs, proteins, and fats. “Recovery will be quicker with good nutrition.”

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

“Stop believing in and celebrating, or promoting ancient traditional myths. It only increases food anxiety and prolongs the disease course, and nothing else. My patients recover quickly because I allow them everything during treatment period. Fried foods, whey proteins, thick fruit smoothies, lean meat and poultry and desserts. It’s all fine.”

Dr Swapnil Sharma, consultant and chief surgeon – liver transplant, hepatobiliary, pancreas and GI onco surgery, Wockhardt Hospitals Mumbai Central, said that in the majority of cases, “there is no medical necessity for people to give up protein or to live solely on plain foods”. “In fact, the liver requires sufficient nutrition in order to repair itself and to aid in recovery. So long as a doctor does not recommend otherwise for a particular liver condition, it is advised to follow a balanced diet which includes protein, complex carbohydrates, healthy fats and fruits and vegetables. Protein can be obtained from foods such as dal, pulses, milk, curd, paneer, eggs, fish or lean meat, all of which help to preserve muscle mass and promote healing,” said Dr Sharma.



Dr Sharma said that jaundice is not a disease in itself. “While the liver is recovering, it keeps on carrying out its various important functions such as metabolism and detoxification. Poor nutrition may slow down the recovery process, cause a loss of muscle and weaken the immune system, thus making it more difficult for the body to recover. Patients can help themselves to recover more comfortably by eating sufficient calories and protein, remaining well hydrated and taking small, frequent meals if their appetite is poor,” said Dr Sharma.

You can have protein (Photo: Freepik) You can have protein (Photo: Freepik)

Should there be any foods that it is genuinely necessary to avoid?

Rather than concentrating on unnecessary restrictions, it is better to steer clear of foods which place extra strain on the body. “Alcohol must be totally avoided until the liver has recovered. Oily, deep-fried and highly processed foods should be limited, not since they directly aggravate jaundice, but because they are difficult to digest and have little nutritional value. It is likewise advisable to avoid food that is unhygienic or water that is contaminated, particularly in the case of viral hepatitis, since it is important there to prevent further infections,” said Dr Sharma.

It can be liver related or non liver related. Acute hepatitis leading to jaundice is the most common cause… https://t.co/yxAdbgz9fw — TheLiverDoc™ (@theliverdoc) July 27, 2026

What to note?

It is a common belief that reducing one’s food intake allows the liver to ‘rest’, but in most cases the situation is the reverse.



“Limiting food without first seeking medical advice may cause the body to lack the nutrients it needs in order to heal. Recovery from jaundice has nothing to do with sticking to a tasteless or very restrictive diet; it is about having a balanced and nutritious diet that satisfies the body’s energy and protein needs. Since each patient is different, dietary recommendations should always be adapted to the specific cause of the jaundice rather than relying on old myths or home remedies.”

World.title: ‘My friends said I look like Hrithik Roshan’: Sourav Das responds to Kangana Ranaut’s remarks
World.content:
The student protest may have ended, but the war of words between actor-politician Kangana Ranaut and CJP spokesperson Saurav Das appears to be just beginning. The two have been locked in a heated exchange after Kangana made a series of harsh remarks about Gen Z protesters, calling them “gutter generation” and describing their videos as “puke-inducing.” Now, Saurav has hit back, saying his friends believe he resembles a younger Hrithik Roshan and suggesting that Kangana’s remarks sounded “frustrated” and were not those of someone who was “mentally stable.”

Speaking to Barkha Dutt on The Mojo Story, Saurav said he had no personal animosity towards the actor and accused Kangana of making the exchange personal. “See, I have nothing personal against Kangana. She is the one using personal remarks against Gen Z and now against me. As I said on my Instagram Story today, ‘Yo, Kangana, just take a chill pill. Let’s talk this out.’ That is how it should be.”

He added that the lack of dialogue had become a major problem in the country. “The problem in this country is that people don’t talk anymore. There is less deliberation, discussion and debate. We should stay within our limits while speaking. That is what I would tell her.”

‘My friends said I look like a young Hrithik Roshan’

Addressing Kangana’s repeated criticism of him, Saurav said his friends had also questioned why the actor-politician appeared to be targeting him. “My friends were texting me and asking, ‘Why is she after your life?’ One of them said that I may look a little like a young Hrithik Roshan. This is what my friends told me. I was pleasantly surprised. Why should someone like her attack someone like me?”

He went on to urge Kangana to be more careful with her words.

“But in any case, be that as it may, I would just say: be careful of your words. Don’t sound frustrated. It is sounding very frustrated. These are not the words or sentences of someone who is mentally stable. Just think before speaking about the future generation of this country because, ultimately, she serves at the pleasure of the people. The government is at the pleasure of the people, and people cannot be disrespected in this manner.”

When asked whether he would be open to having coffee with the MP, Saurav said, “Of course. We harbour no ill will against anybody, including BJP MPs.”



How the Kangana Ranaut-Saurav Das feud began

The exchange began after Saurav strongly criticised Kangana for her comments about Gen Z protesters on Instagram.

Sharing her reaction to videos from the protests, Kangana wrote, “Never in my life have I seen so much ugliness in one place. These reels from Gen Z protests are puke-inducing—the way they speak and the kind of language they are using. Never in my life have I seen everything in every frame so jarring and so crass all at once. Ewwww, who is birthing and raising them?”

She added, “You call yourself cockroaches and look/behave like them as well. There is no paradox or juxtaposition there, just simply subjecting the world to your filth, garbage and ugliness. I am scarred from these reels, need some healing, digital detox.”

Reacting to her remarks, Saurav told ANI, “Even members of her own party don’t pay much heed to Kangana Ranaut or take her seriously, so why should we? I don’t think anyone in Gen Z, Gen Alpha or any younger generation takes her seriously or listens to what she says.”



ALSO READ | Mahima Makwana lived in a chawl, lost father at 5 months, now owns 2 Mumbai homes at 26

He also referred to an earlier video in which Kangana spoke about the workload involved in being a Member of Parliament.

“She is a politician now. There were videos from when she visited her constituency in Himachal Pradesh where she remarked that she had expected the job to require very little work, only to realise that being a Member of Parliament involves a massive amount of labour. That speaks volumes about her own seriousness.”

Kangana later responded to Saurav on Instagram, questioning how he continued to identify himself as a student at the age of 28.



“I just Googled this person and he is 28 years old. And he claims to be a student. How he claims to be a student, I have no clue! At his age, I had two National Awards.” Defending her earlier remarks about being overwhelmed by her responsibilities as an MP, Kangana wrote, “Yes, as a new parliamentarian, I was overwhelmed with all the work because I am also a filmmaker, performing artist, producer, screenwriter and entrepreneur.”

She then launched a personal attack on Saurav, writing, “But someone like him, who is totally useless and unemployed, will never understand what it means to be in massive demand at all times, at any age. Dear Saurav, your issues are personal. You are not a student; you are simply useless. Let’s start with learning some skill. It’s a good place to start.”

World.title: Man held for beating auto driver to death with iron rod in Gurgaon road rage incident
World.content:
A taxi driver was arrested from Delhi on Tuesday for allegedly beating an auto-rickshaw driver to death with an iron rod following a road dispute over giving way in Gurgaon’s Udyog Vihar, police said on Wednesday.

The deceased has been identified as Arvind (32), belonging to Tauli village in Uttar Pradesh’s Raebareli district, an officer said, adding that he was residing in Jharsa in Gurgaon.
